# gh-1570: [GOAL] ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point (TUI + Flutter app)

## Description

## Goal — ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point, TUI and Flutter app alike (v1)

One sentence: **the provider+model pair in fa becomes a single validated identity object** — every way a session picks its model (env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`, `/provider`, session restore, provider queue, media slots, Flutter app settings) produces the whole binding or fails loudly naming both sides; a model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire format, or API key.

Today fa holds the pieces correctly *inside* the resolved world — `ModelRef.parse` requires a provider (`lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`), `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry` assembles model+key+stream from one ref (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`), `FallbackStreamFunction` advances chain entries atomically (`lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`), and `ProviderQueueEntry` carries `{provider_type, provider_config{model, baseUrl, apiKeyEnv}}` (`lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue.dart`). What is missing is the boundary *into* that world: entry points assemble `model` and `provider` from **different sources with no joint validation**, and only `providerKind` is persisted — so a mismatch is invisible at boot, survives restart, and masquerades as "the default provider". A fresh core audit pinned 19 concrete instances (13 core-audit + 4 from the user-flow re-audit + 2 owner-requested: surgical re-auth, multi-instance concurrency) of this one mechanism class (table below), including a real production incident (2026-10-12, bench job 114848402110: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + LAN OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire spoken to an OpenAI endpoint; the trial died before the agent started and the job reported green). This card eliminates the class at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted: "fix the findings one by one."** Nineteen findings that share one mechanism — *identity of a provider is the wire-kind of its spec, not the record the user pointed at; entry points build model and provider from disjoint sources; persistence keeps only `providerKind`* — cannot be converged by nineteen patches. Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. The class dies only when there is exactly one object that *is* a provider+model choice and exactly one validating constructor that produces it.
- **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. Silent defaults here are a credential-leak channel (see Security), not a convenience.
- **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │
 └────┴─────────┴──────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴─────┘
                                   │
                    ProviderModelBinding.resolve(...)   ← core lib/, ONLY constructor
                                   │  validates: wire kind ⇄ endpoint dialect,
                                   │  model ⇄ endpoint catalog, key slot ⇄ endpoint
                                   ▼
        ProviderModelBinding { recordName, providerKind(wire), baseUrl,
                               modelId, keyEnvRef, provenance }
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                              ▼
  session runtime          persisted state (record NAME,      both hosts render
  (roles, queue,           never kind-only)                   identical errors
   media, restore)
```

**Named components**

- **`ProviderModelBinding`** (core `lib/`, new): immutable value object — the complete identity of one provider+model choice: catalog record name (or explicit custom-record id), wire kind, normalized `baseUrl`, `modelId`, key env indirection (never a key value), and provenance (`env` / `flag` / `restore` / `command` / `queue` / `media` / `app`). Single validating constructor `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`; no other code path may construct one.
- **Binding validation rules** (all enforced inside `resolve`, all produce errors naming BOTH the model and the provider/endpoint):
  1. *Wire⇄endpoint*: the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind. An explicit override (e.g. `wire:` key in `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` / config record) is the only escape hatch and is echoed in every report.
  2. *Model⇄endpoint*: a model id is validated against the endpoint's model list when one is available. When the endpoint exposes no list, manual entry is ALWAYS allowed (decided, Q2): the prompt says `enter the model id manually — sent as-is`, the confirmation names the endpoint, and the status bar carries an `unverified` marker until the endpoint confirms the id; headless/non-TTY requires an explicit opt-in flag (`--allow-unverified`) so automation never blocks on a prompt.
  3. *Key⇄endpoint*: the key env indirection is resolved against the binding's own record, with normalized endpoint comparison (`sameEndpoint` semantics, as roles/key_status already use) deciding "custom endpoint" — never a raw string compare.
  4. *No partial overrides*: an entry point that changes only `model` (e.g. `--model` without `--provider`) revalidates the model against the *current* binding and rejects on mismatch; it never silently inherits provider/baseUrl from a different source.
- **BindingStore** (core `lib/`): persists the **record name** (or full custom record) + modelId + normalized baseUrl — never `providerKind` alone. Restart re-resolves the record, so kimi/codemie (which share wire kind `openai-completions`) restore their own catalog env names and endpoints.
- **Host parity layer**: CLI/TUI commands and the Flutter app (`AgentService`, settings UI) call the same `resolve`/`BindingStore` API. `flutter_app/` contains zero binding logic of its own; the shared test suite runs the same scenarios through both hosts.

**Invariants**

- I1: Every session's effective model comes from exactly one `ProviderModelBinding`; no code reads `model` and `provider` from different sources.
- I2: A binding that fails validation never reaches the network layer; the error names model, endpoint, and wire kind.
- I3: A media slot without explicit user configuration is **disabled**; vision/transcribe requests never contain the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire adapter.
- I4: A key resolved for endpoint E is never sent to an endpoint ≠ E (normalized comparison).
- I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.
- I6: TUI and Flutter app produce identical bindings and identical error text for identical inputs.

## Audit findings (all 19, one mechanism class)

| # | Location (path:symbol) | Failure scenario | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | `lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart` : `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` | `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` maps to the anthropic spec kind; `baseUrl` is never validated against the dialect; key `'api'` is unsupported (`_supportedConfigKeys = baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel`). `anthropic` + OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire on an OpenAI endpoint, unfixable via env. **Real incident: bench job 114848402110, 2026-10-12 …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

Today fa holds the pieces correctly *inside* the resolved world — `ModelRef.parse` requires a provider (`lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`), `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry` assembles model+key+stream from one ref (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`), `FallbackStreamFunction` advances chain entries atomically (`lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`), and `ProviderQueueEntry` carries `{provider_type, provider_config{model, baseUrl, apiKeyEnv}}` (`lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue.dart`). What is missing is the boundary *into* that world: entry points assemble `model` and `provider` from **different sources with no joint validation**, and only `providerKind` is persisted — so a mismatch is invisible at boot, survives restart, and masquerades as "the default provider". A fresh core audit pinned 19 concrete instances (13 core-audit + 4 from the user-flow re-audit + 2 owner-requested: surgical re-auth, multi-instance concurrency) of this one mechanism class (table below), including a real production incident (2026-10-12, bench job 114848402110: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + LAN OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire spoken to an OpenAI endpoint; the trial died before the agent started and the job reported green). This card eliminates the class at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted: "fix the findings one by one."** Nineteen findings that share one mechanism — *identity of a provider is the wire-kind of its spec, not the record the user pointed at; entry points build model and provider from disjoint sources; persistence keeps only `providerKind`* — cannot be converged by nineteen patches. Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. The class dies only when there is exactly one object that *is* a provider+model choice and exactly one validating constructor that produces it.
- **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. Silent defaults here are a credential-leak channel (see Security), not a convenience.
- **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │
 └────┴─────────┴──────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴─────┘
                                   │
                    ProviderModelBinding.resolve(...)   ← core lib/, ONLY constructor
                                   │  validates: wire kind ⇄ endpoint dialect,
                                   │  model ⇄ endpoint catalog, key slot ⇄ endpoint
                                   ▼
        ProviderModelBinding { recordName, providerKind(wire), baseUrl,
                               modelId, keyEnvRef, provenance }
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                              ▼
  session runtime          persisted state (record NAME,      both hosts render
  (roles, queue,           never kind-only)                   identical errors
   media, restore)
```

**Named components**

- **`ProviderModelBinding`** (core `lib/`, new): immutable value object — the complete identity of one provider+model choice: catalog record name (or explicit custom-record id), wire kind, normalized `baseUrl`, `modelId`, key env indirection (never a key value), and provenance (`env` / `flag` / `restore` / `command` / `queue` / `media` / `app`). Single validating constructor `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`; no other code path may construct one.
- **Binding validation rules** (all enforced inside `resolve`, all produce errors naming BOTH the model and the provider/endpoint):
  1. *Wire⇄endpoint*: the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind. An explicit override (e.g. `wire:` key in `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` / config record) is the only escape hatch and is echoed in every report.
  2. *Model⇄endpoint*: a model id is validated against the endpoint's model list when one is available. When the endpoint exposes no list, manual entry is ALWAYS allowed (decided, Q2): the prompt says `enter the model id manually — sent as-is`, the confirmation names the endpoint, and the status bar carries an `unverified` marker until the endpoint confirms the id; headless/non-TTY requires an explicit opt-in flag (`--allow-unverified`) so automation never blocks on a prompt.
  3. *Key⇄endpoint*: the key env indirection is resolved against the binding's own record, with normalized endpoint comparison (`sameEndpoint` semantics, as roles/key_status already use) deciding "custom endpoint" — never a raw string compare.
  4. *No partial overrides*: an entry point that changes only `model` (e.g. `--model` without `--provider`) revalidates the model against the *current* binding and rejects on mismatch; it never silently inherits provider/baseUrl from a different source.
- **BindingStore** (core `lib/`): persists the **record name** (or full custom record) + modelId + normalized baseUrl — never `providerKind` alone. Restart re-resolves the record, so kimi/codemie (which share wire kind `openai-completions`) restore their own catalog env names and endpoints.
- **Host parity layer**: CLI/TUI commands and the Flutter app (`AgentService`, settings UI) call the same `resolve`/`BindingStore` API. `flutter_app/` contains zero binding logic of its own; the shared test suite runs the same scenarios through both hosts.

**Invariants**

- I1: Every session's effective model comes from exactly one `ProviderModelBinding`; no code reads `model` and `provider` from different sources.
- I2: A binding that fails validation never reaches the network layer; the error names model, endpoint, and wire kind.
- I3: A media slot without explicit user configuration is **disabled**; vision/transcribe requests never contain the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire adapter.
- I4: A key resolved for endpoint E is never sent to an endpoint ≠ E (normalized comparison).
- I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.
- I6: TUI and Flutter app produce identical bindings and identical error text for identical inputs.

**Core deliverable (the mechanism class fix):**
1. New `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart` (or `lib/src/cli/`?) — `ProviderModelBinding` immutable value object with `resolve` validating constructor:

     - wire⇄endpoint: known dialect vs wire kind, `wire:` override escape hatch
     - no partial overrides: model-only change revalidates against current binding (rejects on mismatch when the model id belongs to a different dialect?) — hmm, this is where it gets tricky. "revalidates the model against the current binding and rejects on mismatch". Model⇄endpoint validation requires knowing which models belong to which endpoint/catalog. The catalog has model lists? Let me check the provider catalog — does it carry model ids per provider?
     
Let me check what model catalog info exists (contextWindows per model id per provider?). Let me grep.

2. **Env preconfig**: add `wire` key support to `_supportedConfigKeys`; validate wire⇄endpoint dialect (the incident: FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic + OpenAI-compatible baseUrl). How do we know a baseUrl is "OpenAI-compatible"? We can't in general — but the ticket says "the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind". Known dialect = if the baseUrl matches a known catalog provider's default endpoint for a DIFFERENT dialect, it's a mismatch. E.g. baseUrl `https://api.z.ai/...` known zai dialect vs wire anthropic → mismatch. The incident: LAN OpenAI proxy — how would we know it's OpenAI-compatible? Hmm, in the incident, `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` model id — the model prefix names the provider `zai`! Model ids with `provider/model` prefix form: `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`, `anthropic/claude-...`, `openai/gpt-...`. OpenRouter-style ids. So model⇄endpoint validation can catch `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` on a wire=anthropic binding: the model id's catalog family is zai (openai-completions wire), mismatching the anthropic wire.

Also baseUrl host matching: if baseUrl host matches a catalog spec's default endpoint host (e.g. api.anthropic.com) but wire kind is openai-completions → mismatch.

So validation rules for wire⇄endpoint:
- if baseUrl matches (normalized/sameEndpoint) any catalog spec's defaultBaseUrl with a different kind → error.
- if modelId has a `<family>/` prefix where family resolves to a catalog spec with a known kind different from the wire kind → error.
- explicit `wire:` override passes, echoed in reports.

That's implementable and testable without network.

Investigation complete and report delivered. Summary of the key facts gathered:

1. **`_switchToCatalogProvider`** (provider_commands.dart L1850–1864) passes `_agent.state.model.id` at **L1863** — the previous provider's model id is re-used, no catalog-default lookup.
2. **Three OpenRouter branches** pass `_agent.state.model.id` into `_switchProvider`: **L991–995** (stored key), **L1034–1039** (API key), **L1209–1215** (OAuth); plus two auxiliary sites at L1055 (wizard `modelId:`) and L1239 (`_saveCatalogConnectEntry`).

# gh-1570: [GOAL] ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point (TUI + Flutter app)

## Description

## Goal — ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point, TUI and Flutter app alike (v1)

One sentence: **the provider+model pair in fa becomes a single validated identity object** — every way a session picks its model (env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`, `/provider`, session restore, provider queue, media slots, Flutter app settings) produces the whole binding or fails loudly naming both sides; a model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire format, or API key.

Today fa holds the pieces correctly *inside* the resolved world — `ModelRef.parse` requires a provider (`lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`), `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry` assembles model+key+stream from one ref (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`), `FallbackStreamFunction` advances chain entries atomically (`lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`), and `ProviderQueueEntry` carries `{provider_type, provider_config{model, baseUrl, apiKeyEnv}}` (`lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue.dart`). What is missing is the boundary *into* that world: entry points assemble `model` and `provider` from **different sources with no joint validation**, and only `providerKind` is persisted — so a mismatch is invisible at boot, survives restart, and masquerades as "the default provider". A fresh core audit pinned 19 concrete instances (13 core-audit + 4 from the user-flow re-audit + 2 owner-requested: surgical re-auth, multi-instance concurrency) of this one mechanism class (table below), including a real production incident (2026-10-12, bench job 114848402110: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + LAN OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire spoken to an OpenAI endpoint; the trial died before the agent started and the job reported green). This card eliminates the class at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted: "fix the findings one by one."** Nineteen findings that share one mechanism — *identity of a provider is the wire-kind of its spec, not the record the user pointed at; entry points build model and provider from disjoint sources; persistence keeps only `providerKind`* — cannot be converged by nineteen patches. Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. The class dies only when there is exactly one object that *is* a provider+model choice and exactly one validating constructor that produces it.
- **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. Silent defaults here are a credential-leak channel (see Security), not a convenience.
- **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │
 └────┴─────────┴──────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴─────┘
                                   │
                    ProviderModelBinding.resolve(...)   ← core lib/, ONLY constructor
                                   │  validates: wire kind ⇄ endpoint dialect,
                                   │  model ⇄ endpoint catalog, key slot ⇄ endpoint
                                   ▼
        ProviderModelBinding { recordName, providerKind(wire), baseUrl,
                               modelId, keyEnvRef, provenance }
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                              ▼
  session runtime          persisted state (record NAME,      both hosts render
  (roles, queue,           never kind-only)                   identical errors
   media, restore)
```

**Named components**

- **`ProviderModelBinding`** (core `lib/`, new): immutable value object — the complete identity of one provider+model choice: catalog record name (or explicit custom-record id), wire kind, normalized `baseUrl`, `modelId`, key env indirection (never a key value), and provenance (`env` / `flag` / `restore` / `command` / `queue` / `media` / `app`). Single validating constructor `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`; no other code path may construct one.
- **Binding validation rules** (all enforced inside `resolve`, all produce errors naming BOTH the model and the provider/endpoint):
  1. *Wire⇄endpoint*: the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind. An explicit override (e.g. `wire:` key in `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` / config record) is the only escape hatch and is echoed in every report.
  2. *Model⇄endpoint*: a model id is validated against the endpoint's model list when one is available. When the endpoint exposes no list, manual entry is ALWAYS allowed (decided, Q2): the prompt says `enter the model id manually — sent as-is`, the confirmation names the endpoint, and the status bar carries an `unverified` marker until the endpoint confirms the id; headless/non-TTY requires an explicit opt-in flag (`--allow-unverified`) so automation never blocks on a prompt.
  3. *Key⇄endpoint*: the key env indirection is resolved against the binding's own record, with normalized endpoint comparison (`sameEndpoint` semantics, as roles/key_status already use) deciding "custom endpoint" — never a raw string compare.
  4. *No partial overrides*: an entry point that changes only `model` (e.g. `--model` without `--provider`) revalidates the model against the *current* binding and rejects on mismatch; it never silently inherits provider/baseUrl from a different source.
- **BindingStore** (core `lib/`): persists the **record name** (or full custom record) + modelId + normalized baseUrl — never `providerKind` alone. Restart re-resolves the record, so kimi/codemie (which share wire kind `openai-completions`) restore their own catalog env names and endpoints.
- **Host parity layer**: CLI/TUI commands and the Flutter app (`AgentService`, settings UI) call the same `resolve`/`BindingStore` API. `flutter_app/` contains zero binding logic of its own; the shared test suite runs the same scenarios through both hosts.

**Invariants**

- I1: Every session's effective model comes from exactly one `ProviderModelBinding`; no code reads `model` and `provider` from different sources.
- I2: A binding that fails validation never reaches the network layer; the error names model, endpoint, and wire kind.
- I3: A media slot without explicit user configuration is **disabled**; vision/transcribe requests never contain the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire adapter.
- I4: A key resolved for endpoint E is never sent to an endpoint ≠ E (normalized comparison).
- I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.
- I6: TUI and Flutter app produce identical bindings and identical error text for identical inputs.

## Audit findings (all 19, one mechanism class)

| # | Location (path:symbol) | Failure scenario | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | `lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart` : `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` | `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` maps to the anthropic spec kind; `baseUrl` is never validated against the dialect; key `'api'` is unsupported (`_supportedConfigKeys = baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel`). `anthropic` + OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire on an OpenAI endpoint, unfixable via env. **Real incident: bench job 114848402110, 2026-10-12 …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

- I3: A media slot without explicit user configuration is **disabled**; vision/transcribe requests never contain the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire adapter.
- I4: A key resolved for endpoint E is never sent to an endpoint ≠ E (normalized comparison).
- I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.

But that risk is exactly what the ticket accepts: for default-endpoint providers the leaf must be applied.

Since a leaf without baseUrl/customProvider carries no endpoint info, applying provider+modelId means binding to the spec's default endpoint. The ticket explicitly wants that for default-endpoint providers (anthropic/google/zai leaves have baseUrl == null).

But for e.g. a kimi session with pre-gh-1000 records (no baseUrl pin), applying would bind to kimi's catalog default endpoint `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`... wait, `resolveCliProviderSpec('openai-completions')` resolves to the openai spec or the legacy openrouter spec. The leaf provider for legacy sessions would be `openai-completions` kind which doesn't uniquely identify kimi. Hmm. The folder state fallback (step 2) handles that via the folder memory. So the change: in step 1, apply the leaf whenever `resolveCliProviderSpec(leafModel.provider) != null` AND the leaf provider kind is NOT the ambiguous `openai-completions` kind without endpoint info (for that kind, keep the folder-state fallback). For unambiguous providers (anthropic, google, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, chatgpt, kimi, codemie, openrouter as names...), apply.

Wait — but what does `leafModel.provider` contain for a `/model claude-x` switch on anthropic provider? It contains the provider KIND (`anthropic`) — `model_change(provider: ...)`. And a leaf from an assistant message contains the model's provider as `Model.provider` — the catalog name or kind. OK.

So the M4 fix in step 1: apply the leaf binding when the spec resolves and (baseUrl != null || customProvider != null || spec.kind is endpoint-unambiguous). Where endpoint-unambiguous means: resolving `leafModel.provider` yields a spec whose default endpoint IS the serving endpoint (i.e., no baseUrl pin needed because there's only one endpoint for that identity), e.g. `anthropic` → `https://api.anthropic.com`. But careful: anthropic-kind model could be served via a custom proxy baseUrl — with no pin we can't know. The ticket accepts binding to the default endpoint in that case? "AC5 — Session restore pins the full binding for default-endpoint providers too; a claude session never resumes on the boot model". Yes — for default-endpoint providers the leaf must apply. If the session ran on a proxy, the model_change record from the switch would have pinned baseUrl (since gh-1000). Legacy pre-gh-1000 sessions on proxies are edge; the ticket prioritizes the claude-on-copilot failure.

And "absent state is a clean error, not a silent fallback" — when neither leaf nor folder state exists... today `state == null → return` silently keeps the boot model. AC5 says: a claude session never resumes on the boot model; absent state is a clean error. Hmm, but that would break restoring old sessions that never recorded model state (boot model is right for them). The "absent state" refers to when the session leaf says provider X but...? Actually re-reading: "Session restore pins the full binding for default-endpoint providers too; a claude session never resumes on the boot model; absent state is a clean error, not a silent fallback." I think this refers to the case where a session has a leaf model pin that can't be satisfied. But making absent folder state a hard error for ALL sessions would break the legacy behavior for brand-new sessions... Actually no: for a NEW session there's no leaf either. The case is: `--session` restore where the leaf has a model pin. If leaf provider is unresolvable AND folder state absent → currently silent boot-model fallback. AC5 wants a clean error/note. I'll make it a loud note (writeln) rather than a hard error — hmm, "absent state is a clean error". For the TUI, a hard error mid-restore might brick resume. The doc says "never silent". A named warning line satisfies "clean error, not silent fallback" while keeping the boot usable... but the AC text says "absent state is a clean error". Risky. Let me be pragmatic: keep restore functional but LOUD — print a named note that the session's binding is absent and the boot default stands. Hmm, but the acceptance test UT-5 says "absent state ⇒ error not fallback".

Let me look at how the boot (bin/fah.dart) does the folder-model-state application, and what a "clean error" would mean there. Actually, maybe the right reading: for a leaf pin that names a provider no version knows (spec == null) AND no folder state → clean error naming the session's provider instead of silently resuming on the boot model. I'll implement: if a leaf model pin exists but is unresolvable and no folder state resolves → print a loud named error note (io.writeln with `error:` prefix...). Hmm — actually for the CLI restore path in bin/fah.dart, a ConfigException would abort the boot. For --session resume, aborting the boot on a stale pin is hostile. The ticket's phrase "absent state is a clean error, not a silent fallback" — I'll implement a loud, named stderr/writeln error line and keep the boot model. That's "clean error" (named, actionable) without bricking.

OK. Now let me check the remaining pieces: `_judgeSavedRestore` L9 — endpoint conflict degrades kind to openai-completions keeping stale baseUrl+model. Let me re-read the restore: `restoredKind = restore.endpointConflict ? null : restore.spec?.kind` → provider falls back to parsed default. Then `baseUrl = parsed.baseUrl ?? faPreconfig?.baseUrl ?? saved.baseUrl` — the STALE baseUrl from the saved config is still applied even when the provider degrades! And `modelId` too. That's L9: "On endpoint conflict the kind degrades to openai-completions but the stale baseUrl+model are kept — degradation preserves the poison." Fix: when endpointConflict and no explicit override, drop the saved baseUrl and modelId too (fall to parsed defaults), matching the degraded provider. E2: "degraded kind must not inherit stale baseUrl+model; restore either rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly".

Now H2 (AC3): explicit `--model` without `--provider`: `modelId = parsed.model ?? ...` while provider comes from saved. Fix: when parsed.model is explicit and the resolved provider (saved) mismatches the model's family → ConfigException naming both sides. How to detect mismatch: model id family prefix (`gpt-5` has no prefix; `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` has prefix `zai`). For unprefixed ids we can use `remoteCatalogEnrichment` or model-family heuristics? The ticket's scenario: "Yesterday anthropic → today `fa -p "fix" --model gpt-5`". gpt-5 — how do we know gpt-5 is not anthropic model? There might be a catalog of models with providers. Let me check remote_catalog / model catalog in lib/src/model_roles/. There's `remoteCatalogEnrichment.chatFallbackFor(spec.kind)` mentioned by the explorer. Let me grep for a model→provider mapping.

Actually the practical validation: the `ProviderModelBinding.resolve` should validate model⇄wire via:
1. explicit family prefix in model id (`vendor/model`): resolve vendor through the catalog → compare kinds.
2. baseUrl matching a known catalog spec's default endpoint with a different kind.
3. Known-model catalog lookup: if the model id is in the catalog under a provider with a different wire kind → mismatch. Does such a model catalog exist? Let me grep for `remoteCatalogEnrichment` and any static model table.

Let me search the model_roles directory.

# gh-1570: [GOAL] ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point (TUI + Flutter app)

## Description

## Goal — ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point, TUI and Flutter app alike (v1)

One sentence: **the provider+model pair in fa becomes a single validated identity object** — every way a session picks its model (env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`, `/provider`, session restore, provider queue, media slots, Flutter app settings) produces the whole binding or fails loudly naming both sides; a model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire format, or API key.

Today fa holds the pieces correctly *inside* the resolved world — `ModelRef.parse` requires a provider (`lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`), `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry` assembles model+key+stream from one ref (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`), `FallbackStreamFunction` advances chain entries atomically (`lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`), and `ProviderQueueEntry` carries `{provider_type, provider_config{model, baseUrl, apiKeyEnv}}` (`lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue.dart`). What is missing is the boundary *into* that world: entry points assemble `model` and `provider` from **different sources with no joint validation**, and only `providerKind` is persisted — so a mismatch is invisible at boot, survives restart, and masquerades as "the default provider". A fresh core audit pinned 19 concrete instances (13 core-audit + 4 from the user-flow re-audit + 2 owner-requested: surgical re-auth, multi-instance concurrency) of this one mechanism class (table below), including a real production incident (2026-10-12, bench job 114848402110: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + LAN OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire spoken to an OpenAI endpoint; the trial died before the agent started and the job reported green). This card eliminates the class at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted: "fix the findings one by one."** Nineteen findings that share one mechanism — *identity of a provider is the wire-kind of its spec, not the record the user pointed at; entry points build model and provider from disjoint sources; persistence keeps only `providerKind`* — cannot be converged by nineteen patches. Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. The class dies only when there is exactly one object that *is* a provider+model choice and exactly one validating constructor that produces it.
- **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. Silent defaults here are a credential-leak channel (see Security), not a convenience.
- **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │
 └────┴─────────┴──────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴─────┘
                                   │
                    ProviderModelBinding.resolve(...)   ← core lib/, ONLY constructor
                                   │  validates: wire kind ⇄ endpoint dialect,
                                   │  model ⇄ endpoint catalog, key slot ⇄ endpoint
                                   ▼
        ProviderModelBinding { recordName, providerKind(wire), baseUrl,
                               modelId, keyEnvRef, provenance }
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                              ▼
  session runtime          persisted state (record NAME,      both hosts render
  (roles, queue,           never kind-only)                   identical errors
   media, restore)
```

**Named components**

- **`ProviderModelBinding`** (core `lib/`, new): immutable value object — the complete identity of one provider+model choice: catalog record name (or explicit custom-record id), wire kind, normalized `baseUrl`, `modelId`, key env indirection (never a key value), and provenance (`env` / `flag` / `restore` / `command` / `queue` / `media` / `app`). Single validating constructor `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`; no other code path may construct one.
- **Binding validation rules** (all enforced inside `resolve`, all produce errors naming BOTH the model and the provider/endpoint):
  1. *Wire⇄endpoint*: the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind. An explicit override (e.g. `wire:` key in `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` / config record) is the only escape hatch and is echoed in every report.
  2. *Model⇄endpoint*: a model id is validated against the endpoint's model list when one is available. When the endpoint exposes no list, manual entry is ALWAYS allowed (decided, Q2): the prompt says `enter the model id manually — sent as-is`, the confirmation names the endpoint, and the status bar carries an `unverified` marker until the endpoint confirms the id; headless/non-TTY requires an explicit opt-in flag (`--allow-unverified`) so automation never blocks on a prompt.
  3. *Key⇄endpoint*: the key env indirection is resolved against the binding's own record, with normalized endpoint comparison (`sameEndpoint` semantics, as roles/key_status already use) deciding "custom endpoint" — never a raw string compare.
  4. *No partial overrides*: an entry point that changes only `model` (e.g. `--model` without `--provider`) revalidates the model against the *current* binding and rejects on mismatch; it never silently inherits provider/baseUrl from a different source.
- **BindingStore** (core `lib/`): persists the **record name** (or full custom record) + modelId + normalized baseUrl — never `providerKind` alone. Restart re-resolves the record, so kimi/codemie (which share wire kind `openai-completions`) restore their own catalog env names and endpoints.
- **Host parity layer**: CLI/TUI commands and the Flutter app (`AgentService`, settings UI) call the same `resolve`/`BindingStore` API. `flutter_app/` contains zero binding logic of its own; the shared test suite runs the same scenarios through both hosts.

**Invariants**

- I1: Every session's effective model comes from exactly one `ProviderModelBinding`; no code reads `model` and `provider` from different sources.
- I2: A binding that fails validation never reaches the network layer; the error names model, endpoint, and wire kind.
- I3: A media slot without explicit user configuration is **disabled**; vision/transcribe requests never contain the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire adapter.
- I4: A key resolved for endpoint E is never sent to an endpoint ≠ E (normalized comparison).
- I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.
- I6: TUI and Flutter app produce identical bindings and identical error text for identical inputs.

## Audit findings (all 19, one mechanism class)

| # | Location (path:symbol) | Failure scenario | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | `lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart` : `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` | `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` maps to the anthropic spec kind; `baseUrl` is never validated against the dialect; key `'api'` is unsupported (`_supportedConfigKeys = baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel`). `anthropic` + OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire on an OpenAI endpoint, unfixable via env. **Real incident: bench job 114848402110, 2026-10-12 …

factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

One sentence: **the provider+model pair in fa becomes a single validated identity object** — every way a session picks its model (env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`, `/provider`, session restore, provider queue, media slots, Flutter app settings) produces the whole binding or fails loudly naming both sides; a model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire format, or API key.

A fresh core audit pinned 19 concrete instances (13 core-audit + 4 from the user-flow re-audit + 2 owner-requested: surgical re-auth, multi-instance concurrency) of this one mechanism class (table below), including a real production incident (2026-10-12, bench job 114848402110: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + LAN OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire spoken to an OpenAI endpoint; the trial died before the agent started and the job reported green). This card eliminates the class at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted: "fix the findings one by one."** Nineteen findings that share one mechanism — *identity of a provider is the wire-kind of its spec, not the record the user pointed at; entry points build model and provider from disjoint sources; persistence keeps only `providerKind`* — cannot be converged by nineteen patches. Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. - **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. - **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │
 └────┴─────────┴──────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴─────┘
                                   │
                    ProviderModelBinding.resolve(...)   ← core lib/, ONLY constructor
                                   │  validates: wire kind ⇄ endpoint dialect,
                                   │  model ⇄ endpoint catalog, key slot ⇄ endpoint
                                   ▼
        ProviderModelBinding { recordName, providerKind(wire), baseUrl,
                               modelId, keyEnvRef, provenance }
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                              ▼
  session runtime          persisted state (record NAME,      both hosts render
  (roles, queue,           never kind-only)                   identical errors
   media, restore)
```

**Named components**

- **`ProviderModelBinding`** (core `lib/`, new): immutable value object — the complete identity of one provider+model choice: catalog record name (or explicit custom-record id), wire kind, normalized `baseUrl`, `modelId`, key env indirection (never a key value), and provenance (`env` / `flag` / `restore` / `command` / `queue` / `media` / `app`). - **Binding validation rules** (all enforced inside `resolve`, all produce errors naming BOTH the model and the provider/endpoint):

  2. *Model⇄endpoint*: a model id is validated against the endpoint's model list when one is available. - I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.
- I6: TUI and Flutter app produce identical bindings and identical error text for identical inputs.

# gh-1570: [GOAL] ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point (TUI + Flutter app)

## Description

## Goal — ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point, TUI and Flutter app alike (v1)

One sentence: **the provider+model pair in fa becomes a single validated identity object** — every way a session picks its model (env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`, `/provider`, session restore, provider queue, media slots, Flutter app settings) produces the whole binding or fails loudly naming both sides; a model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire format, or API key.

Today fa holds the pieces correctly *inside* the resolved world — `ModelRef.parse` requires a provider (`lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`), `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry` assembles model+key+stream from one ref (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`), `FallbackStreamFunction` advances chain entries atomically (`lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`), and `ProviderQueueEntry` carries `{provider_type, provider_config{model, baseUrl, apiKeyEnv}}` (`lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue.dart`). What is missing is the boundary *into* that world: entry points assemble `model` and `provider` from **different sources with no joint validation**, and only `providerKind` is persisted — so a mismatch is invisible at boot, survives restart, and masquerades as "the default provider". A fresh core audit pinned 19 concrete instances (13 core-audit + 4 from the user-flow re-audit + 2 owner-requested: surgical re-auth, multi-instance concurrency) of this one mechanism class (table below), including a real production incident (2026-10-12, bench job 114848402110: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + LAN OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire spoken to an OpenAI endpoint; the trial died before the agent started and the job reported green). This card eliminates the class at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted: "fix the findings one by one."** Nineteen findings that share one mechanism — *identity of a provider is the wire-kind of its spec, not the record the user pointed at; entry points build model and provider from disjoint sources; persistence keeps only `providerKind`* — cannot be converged by nineteen patches. Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. The class dies only when there is exactly one object that *is* a provider+model choice and exactly one validating constructor that produces it.
- **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. Silent defaults here are a credential-leak channel (see Security), not a convenience.
- **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │
 └────┴─────────┴──────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴─────┘
                                   │
                    ProviderModelBinding.resolve(...)   ← core lib/, ONLY constructor
                                   │  validates: wire kind ⇄ endpoint dialect,
                                   │  model ⇄ endpoint catalog, key slot ⇄ endpoint
                                   ▼
        ProviderModelBinding { recordName, providerKind(wire), baseUrl,
                               modelId, keyEnvRef, provenance }
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                              ▼
  session runtime          persisted state (record NAME,      both hosts render
  (roles, queue,           never kind-only)                   identical errors
   media, restore)
```

**Named components**

- **`ProviderModelBinding`** (core `lib/`, new): immutable value object — the complete identity of one provider+model choice: catalog record name (or explicit custom-record id), wire kind, normalized `baseUrl`, `modelId`, key env indirection (never a key value), and provenance (`env` / `flag` / `restore` / `command` / `queue` / `media` / `app`). Single validating constructor `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`; no other code path may construct one.
- **Binding validation rules** (all enforced inside `resolve`, all produce errors naming BOTH the model and the provider/endpoint):

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…
