# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd

Known dialect = if the baseUrl matches a known catalog provider's default endpoint for a DIFFERENT dialect, it's a mismatch. E.g. baseUrl `https://api.z.ai/...` known zai dialect vs wire anthropic → mismatch. The incident: LAN OpenAI proxy — how would we know it's OpenAI-compatible? Also baseUrl host matching: if baseUrl host matches a catalog spec's default endpoint host (e.g. api.anthropic.com) but wire kind is openai-completions → mismatch.

- if baseUrl matches (normalized/sameEndpoint) any catalog spec's defaultBaseUrl with a different kind → error.

# gh-1570: [GOAL] ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point (TUI + Flutter app)

## Description

## Goal — ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point, TUI and Flutter app alike (v1)

One sentence: **the provider+model pair in fa becomes a single validated identity object** — every way a session picks its model (env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`, `/provider`, session restore, provider queue, media slots, Flutter app settings) produces the whole binding or fails loudly naming both sides; a model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire format, or API key.

Today fa holds the pieces correctly *inside* the resolved world — `ModelRef.parse` requires a provider (`lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`), `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry` assembles model+key+stream from one ref (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`), `FallbackStreamFunction` advances chain entries atomically (`lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`), and `ProviderQueueEntry` carries `{provider_type, provider_config{model, baseUrl, apiKeyEnv}}` (`lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue.dart`). What is missing is the boundary *into* that world: entry points assemble `model` and `provider` from **different sources with no joint validation**, and only `providerKind` is persisted — so a mismatch is invisible at boot, survives restart, and masquerades as "the default provider". A fresh core audit pinned 19 concrete instances (13 core-audit + 4 from the user-flow re-audit + 2 owner-requested: surgical re-auth, multi-instance concurrency) of this one mechanism class (table below), including a real production incident (2026-10-12, bench job 114848402110: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + LAN OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire spoken to an OpenAI endpoint; the trial died before the agent started and the job reported green). This card eliminates the class at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted: "fix the findings one by one."** Nineteen findings that share one mechanism — *identity of a provider is the wire-kind of its spec, not the record the user pointed at; entry points build model and provider from disjoint sources; persistence keeps only `providerKind`* — cannot be converged by nineteen patches. Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. The class dies only when there is exactly one object that *is* a provider+model choice and exactly one validating constructor that produces it.
- **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. Silent defaults here are a credential-leak channel (see Security), not a convenience.
- **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
`/settings` is the interactive settings hub: a TUI picker whose entries
  (Provider, Edit/delete provider, Chat model, Model parameters, Media
  models, Agent models, Approval mode, Agent mode, API keys, MCP servers)
  launch the same flows the dedicated slash commands open; line mode prints
  a summary. ALL TUI pickers (generic host pickers included) have
  type-to-filter + backspace (generic ones filter their static item list
  locally via `menuAllItems`, the models picker rebuilds through
  `buildModelMenu`; a no-match filter keeps the title + `(no matches)`).
  The `/model` TUI menu is TWO-STEP when several providers exist:
  `_buildModelMenu` returns provider rows (`@<name>` keys, the filter
  matches provider names AND their model ids) first, and selecting one
  opens that provider's model list (generic `modelProvider` picker whose
  `provider|model` rows route back through `_tuiSelectModel`'s
  cross-provider switch). A single provider goes straight to its models.
  Model rows render as a TABLE (`buildModelPickerTable` in
  `model_picker_table.dart`): `● id  provider  ctx  cost` with the
  context window compacted (1048576 → `1M`) and `$/Mtok` from the catalog
  (`—` when pricing is unknown, never 0.00); rows sort recency → cheaper
  total → unpriced last; narrow widths elide cost first, then provider,
  keeping id + ctx. The rows are click targets (hit-region routing).
  The provider→model pick flows live in `lib/src/cli/settings_flow.dart` in the
  NAMED `SettingsFlow` extension (public `runProviderModelFlow`/
  `startChatModelFlow`/`startMediaSlotFlow`/`startAgentModelFlow`), so
  tests can drive them line-mode (see `test/cli/settings_flow_test.dart`).
  The model-list fetch dispatches per dialect
  (`_fetchProviderModelIds`: CodeMie `/llm_models` by URL marker, DIAL
  deployments when the spec is `dial`, else OpenAI `/models`; the saved
  entry's own key authenticates; failures fall back to manual entry).
  `startAgentModelFlow` pins the `smol`/`subagent` role chains through
  `ModelRolesResolver.setRoleChain`/`clearRoleChain` (the resolver is
  created on demand when the config had no `roles:` section —
  `AgentCliConfig.modelRolesResolver` is mutable) and persists via
  `onModelsConfigChanged` (bin/fah.dart's persistConfig reads the live
  resolver config).
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles (issue #8): strict `CubeSpec`
  YAML (`.fah/cubes/<name>.yaml`, apiVersion fa/v1 kind Cube) with
  tool/network/fs/env/resource/cache policies (deny-wins, empty allowlist =
  deny-all, lexical path normalization as traversal guard), `CubeResolver`
  (path > name lookup), Dart-layer enforcement (`SandboxedExecutionEnv`
  decorator: `CubeFsGuard` gates the agent's own read/edit/write tools,
  `CubePolicyEngine` gates bash incl. pipes/`$(...)` subshells and shell
  redirect targets (`>`/`>>`/`<>`/`&>`/`2>` writes, `<` reads, `2>&1`
  exempt; arguments stay name-gated only), exit 127
  denials with per-exec reason), content-addressed `CubeCacheManager` under
  `.fah/cube-cache/<md5>/` (manifest + ttl). `spec.backend:` = `policy`
  (default, Dart-only) | `kernel` opt-in: every command wrapped in the OS
  sandbox via `CubeSandboxBackend.wrapCommand` — macOS `sandbox-exec -f
  <profile>`, Linux `unshare --user --map-root-user --mount [--net iff the
  spec allows no network]` + `ulimit -v/-t` ceilings, both over a clean
  `env -i` environment; profiles staged content-verified under
  `<home>/.fah/cube-profiles/<md5>.sb` (outside the guest-writable
  workspace; re-verified against the recomputed profile before every
  wrapped exec — #790); kernel mode fail-closes (`fa_cube[<name>]:`
  error, no exec) when the staging location is not provably
  guest-unwritable — a `homeDir` inside/relative-to the workspace or a
  spec mount granting rw over it (the refusal names
  `spec.allowDegrade: true` as the explicit policy-mode escape hatch;
  with it set, the bind degrades and `onDegrade` fires); the staging
  dir is swept once per
  binding for this profile's own `.tmp` orphans (other bindings' files
  untouched); the macOS SBPL profile denies writes blanket outside the
  workspace + `rw` mounts (`/dev/null`, `/dev/fd` exempt) and denies reads
  of `/etc` + user homes when no root mount grants reads (a blanket read
  deny would abort exec — dyld); Windows = Job Object descriptor only
  (kernel on a platform without an enforcing backend is REFUSED — clean
  `fa_cube[<name>]:` error naming `spec.allowDegrade`, zero commands —
  unless the spec opts in via `allowDegrade: true`, which degrades to
  policy mode with the loud `fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unavailable,
  running in policy mode` warning; `effectiveBackend` reports what
  actually ran — #793); a wrapper that is missing from
  PATH or refuses the sandbox (EPERM, SBPL
  rejection) surfaces as a clean `fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend ...`
  spawn error in foreground execs and background jobs alike. CLI:
  startup precedence flags > project `.fah/config.yaml` `cube:` > user
  config (`resolveStartupCubeSource`), `/settings` Cube sandbox picker
  (shared switch logic in `agent_cli_cube.dart`, persists the `cube:`
  startup default), `/cube [use <name>|off|reload|list|cache status|cache
  clear]`; cache restore at run start + save at end, headless included.
  `SharedSetting.cubeSandbox` is cli-only (host process sandboxing; app
  shells already confined). Contract + reference: `schema/cube_schema.json`
  and `docs/cubes.md`; mock-LLM integration suite
  `test/integration/fa_cube_integration_test.dart` (8 scenarios,
  `--tags integration`).
- `lib/src/prompts/prompt_overrides.dart` — `prompts:` config section maps
  prompt names to file path or inline text; strict validation; flags
  `--system-prompt(-file)` > config > built-in.
- `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart` — full `fah --help` text, guarded by
  `test/cli/cli_help_test.dart` (update BOTH).
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → Brave/Tavily keyed)
  and `web_fetch` (HTML→markdown, pub.dev handler) via
  `builtinTools(env, webSearch:)`.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_catalog.dart` — provider table (incl. the
  `chatgpt` Codex-backend entry, kind `chatgpt-codex`); specs

The condition exists because an assistant-message-derived model pin (which carries no baseUrl) shouldn't force a provider re-switch...? Let me think.

`SessionContext.model` comes from the last `model_change` record OR assistant message. An assistant-message-derived model carries no baseUrl/customProvider. If we applied those, every session restored under a different boot default would force-switch to the leaf's provider — which is exactly what AC5 wants ("a claude session never resumes on the boot model")! Wait, but M4 says "for default-endpoint providers (anthropic/google/zai) the leaf is ignored → fallback to per-folder model-state.json (best-effort, may silently be absent) → a claude session resumes on the boot model (e.g. copilot)".

So the fix per AC5: "Session restore pins the full binding for default-endpoint providers too; a claude session never resumes on the boot model; absent state is a clean error, not a silent fallback."

So the leaf model_change should be applied when provider+modelId resolve, even without baseUrl/customProvider pins. The current guard exists because assistant-message-derived pins might be noisy? Let me check where SessionContext.model gets set from model_change vs assistant message. In session_tree.dart. The leaf model from a `model_change` record is authoritative; from an assistant message it's the model that generated the last message, which is also the effective model actually... Let me look at how context.model is built to distinguish. Actually the safest approach aligned with the ticket: apply the leaf binding when the leaf provider kind differs from the current provider kind OR the model id differs, whenever the leaf provider resolves through the catalog — i.e., always apply when resolvable. # gh-1570: [GOAL] ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point (TUI + Flutter app)

## Description

## Goal — ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point, TUI and Flutter app alike (v1)

One sentence: **the provider+model pair in fa becomes a single validated identity object** — every way a session picks its model (env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`, `/provider`, session restore, provider queue, media slots, Flutter app settings) produces the whole binding or fails loudly naming both sides; a model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire format, or API key.

Today fa holds the pieces correctly *inside* the resolved world — `ModelRef.parse` requires a provider (`lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`), `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry` assembles model+key+stream from one ref (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`), `FallbackStreamFunction` advances chain entries atomically (`lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`), and `ProviderQueueEntry` carries `{provider_type, provider_config{model, baseUrl, apiKeyEnv}}` (`lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue.dart`). What is missing is the boundary *into* that world: entry points assemble `model` and `provider` from **different sources with no joint validation**, and only `providerKind` is persisted — so a mismatch is invisible at boot, survives restart, and masquerades as "the default provider". A fresh core audit pinned 19 concrete instances (13 core-audit + 4 from the user-flow re-audit + 2 owner-requested: surgical re-auth, multi-instance concurrency) of this one mechanism class (table below), including a real production incident (2026-10-12, bench job 114848402110: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + LAN OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire spoken to an OpenAI endpoint; the trial died before the agent started and the job reported green). This card eliminates the class at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted: "fix the findings one by one."** Nineteen findings that share one mechanism — *identity of a provider is the wire-kind of its spec, not the record the user pointed at; entry points build model and provider from disjoint sources; persistence keeps only `providerKind`* — cannot be converged by nineteen patches. Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. The class dies only when there is exactly one object that *is* a provider+model choice and exactly one validating constructor that produces it.
- **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. Silent defaults here are a credential-leak channel (see Security), not a convenience.
- **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │
 └────┴─────────┴──────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴─────┘
                                   │
                    ProviderModelBinding.resolve(...)   ← core lib/, ONLY constructor
                                   │  validates: wire kind ⇄ endpoint dialect,
                                   │  model ⇄ endpoint catalog, key slot ⇄ endpoint
                                   ▼
        ProviderModelBinding { recordName, providerKind(wire), baseUrl,
                               modelId, keyEnvRef, provenance }
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                              ▼
  session runtime          persisted state (record NAME,      both hosts render
  (roles, queue,           never kind-only)                   identical errors
   media, restore)
```

**Named components**

- **`ProviderModelBinding`** (core `lib/`, new): immutable value object — the complete identity of one provider+model choice: catalog record name (or explicit custom-record id), wire kind, normalized `baseUrl`, `modelId`, key env indirection (never a key value), and provenance (`env` / `flag` / `restore` / `command` / `queue` / `media` / `app`). Single validating constructor `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`; no other code path may construct one.
- **Binding validation rules** (all enforced inside `resolve`, all produce errors naming BOTH the model and the provider/endpoint):
  1. *Wire⇄endpoint*: the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind. An explicit override (e.g. `wire:` key in `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` / config record) is the only escape hatch and is echoed in every report.
  2. *Model⇄endpoint*: a model id is validated against the endpoint's model list when one is available. When the endpoint exposes no list, manual entry is ALWAYS allowed (decided, Q2): the prompt says `enter the model id manually — sent as-is`, the confirmation names the endpoint, and the status bar carries an `unverified` marker until the endpoint confirms the id; headless/non-TTY requires an explicit opt-in flag (`--allow-unverified`) so automation never blocks on a prompt.
  3. *Key⇄endpoint*: the key env indirection is resolved against the binding's own record, with normalized endpoint comparison (`sameEndpoint` semantics, as roles/key_status already use) deciding "custom endpoint" — never a raw string compare.
  4. *No partial overrides*: an entry point that changes only `model` (e.g. `--model` without `--provider`) revalidates the model against the *current* binding and rejects on mismatch; it never silently inherits provider/baseUrl from a different source.
- **BindingStore** (core `lib/`): persists the **record name** (or full custom record) + modelId + normalized baseUrl — never `providerKind` alone. Restart re-resolves the record, so kimi/codemie (which share wire kind `openai-completions`) restore their own catalog env names and endpoints.
- **Host parity layer**: CLI/TUI commands and the Flutter app (`AgentService`, settings UI) call the same `resolve`/`BindingStore` API. `flutter_app/` contains zero binding logic of its own; the shared test suite runs the same scenarios through both hosts.

**Invariants**

- I1: Every session's effective model comes from exactly one `ProviderModelBinding`; no code reads `model` and `provider` from different sources.
- I2: A binding that fails validation never reaches the network layer; the error names model, endpoint, and wire kind.
- I3: A media slot without explicit user configuration is **disabled**; vision/transcribe requests never contain the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire adapter.
- I4: A key resolved for endpoint E is never sent to an endpoint ≠ E (normalized comparison).
- I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.
- I6: TUI and Flutter app produce identical bindings and identical error text for identical inputs.

## Audit findings (all 19, one mechanism class)

| # | Location (path:symbol) | Failure scenario | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | `lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart` : `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` | `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` maps to the anthropic spec kind; `baseUrl` is never validated against the dialect; key `'api'` is unsupported (`_supportedConfigKeys = baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel`). `anthropic` + OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire on an OpenAI endpoint, unfixable via env. **Real incident: bench job 114848402110, 2026-10-12 …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

- I3: A media slot without explicit user configuration is **disabled**; vision/transcribe requests never contain the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire adapter.
- I4: A key resolved for endpoint E is never sent to an endpoint ≠ E (normalized comparison).
- I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it

  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run

  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);

  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap

Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. The class dies only when there is exactly one object that *is* a provider+model choice and exactly one validating constructor that produces it.
- **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. Silent defaults here are a credential-leak channel (see Security), not a convenience.
- **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │
 └────┴─────────┴──────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴─────┘
                                   │
                    ProviderModelBinding.resolve(...)   ← core lib/, ONLY constructor
                                   │  validates: wire kind ⇄ endpoint dialect,
                                   │  model ⇄ endpoint catalog, key slot ⇄ endpoint
                                   ▼
        ProviderModelBinding { recordName, providerKind(wire), baseUrl,
                               modelId, keyEnvRef, provenance }
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                              ▼
  session runtime          persisted state (record NAME,      both hosts render
  (roles, queue,           never kind-only)                   identical errors
   media, restore)
```

**Named components**

- **`ProviderModelBinding`** (core `lib/`, new): immutable value object — the complete identity of one provider+model choice: catalog record name (or explicit custom-record id), wire kind, normalized `baseUrl`, `modelId`, key env indirection (never a key value), and provenance (`env` / `flag` / `restore` / `command` / `queue` / `media` / `app`). Single validating constructor `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`; no other code path may construct one.
- **Binding validation rules** (all enforced inside `resolve`, all produce errors naming BOTH the model and the provider/endpoint):
  1. *Wire⇄endpoint*: the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind. An explicit override (e.g. `wire:` key in `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` / config record) is the only escape hatch and is echoed in every report.
  2. *Model⇄endpoint*: a model id is validated against the endpoint's model list when one is available. When the endpoint exposes no list, manual entry is ALWAYS allowed (decided, Q2): the prompt says `enter the model id manually — sent as-is`, the confirmation names the endpoint, and the status bar carries an `unverified` marker until the endpoint confirms the id; headless/non-TTY requires an explicit opt-in flag (`--allow-unverified`) so automation never blocks on a prompt.
  3. *Key⇄endpoint*: the key env indirection is resolved against the binding's own record, with normalized endpoint comparison (`sameEndpoint` semantics, as roles/key_status already use) deciding "custom endpoint" — never a raw string compare.
  4. *No partial overrides*: an entry point that changes only `model` (e.g. `--model` without `--provider`) revalidates the model against the *current* binding and rejects on mismatch; it never silently inherits provider/baseUrl from a different source.
- **BindingStore** (core `lib/`): persists the **record name** (or full custom record) + modelId + normalized baseUrl — never `providerKind` alone. Restart re-resolves the record, so kimi/codemie (which share wire kind `openai-completions`) restore their own catalog env names and endpoints.
- **Host parity layer**: CLI/TUI commands and the Flutter app (`AgentService`, settings UI) call the same `resolve`/`BindingStore` API. `flutter_app/` contains zero binding logic of its own; the shared test suite runs the same scenarios through both hosts.

**Invariants**

- I1: Every session's effective model comes from exactly one `ProviderModelBinding`; no code reads `model` and `provider` from different sources.
- I2: A binding that fails validation never reaches the network layer; the error names model, endpoint, and wire kind.
- I3: A media slot without explicit user configuration is **disabled**; vision/transcribe requests never contain the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire adapter.
- I4: A key resolved for endpoint E is never sent to an endpoint ≠ E (normalized comparison).
- I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.
- I6: TUI and Flutter app produce identical bindings and identical error text for identical inputs.

{
  "key": "gh-1570",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point (TUI + Flutter app)",
    "description": "## Goal — ProviderModelBinding: one validated provider+model identity across every entry point, TUI and Flutter app alike (v1)

One sentence: **the provider+model pair in fa becomes a single validated identity object** — every way a session picks its model (env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`, `/provider`, session restore, provider queue, media slots, Flutter app settings) produces the whole binding or fails loudly naming both sides; a model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire format, or API key.

Today fa holds the pieces correctly *inside* the resolved world — `ModelRef.parse` requires a provider (`lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`), `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry` assembles model+key+stream from one ref (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`), `FallbackStreamFunction` advances chain entries atomically (`lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`), and `ProviderQueueEntry` carries `{provider_type, provider_config{model, baseUrl, apiKeyEnv}}` (`lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue.dart`). What is missing is the boundary *into* that world: entry points assemble `model` and `provider` from **different sources with no joint validation**, and only `providerKind` is persisted — so a mismatch is invisible at boot, survives restart, and masquerades as "the default provider". A fresh core audit pinned 19 concrete instances (13 core-audit + 4 from the user-flow re-audit + 2 owner-requested: surgical re-auth, multi-instance concurrency) of this one mechanism class (table below), including a real production incident (2026-10-12, bench job 114848402110: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + LAN OpenAI-compatible proxy + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` → anthropic wire spoken to an OpenAI endpoint; the trial died before the agent started and the job reported green). This card eliminates the class at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted: "fix the findings one by one."** Nineteen findings that share one mechanism — *identity of a provider is the wire-kind of its spec, not the record the user pointed at; entry points build model and provider from disjoint sources; persistence keeps only `providerKind`* — cannot be converged by nineteen patches. Each local fix leaves the other eighteen entry points free to reintroduce the class. The class dies only when there is exactly one object that *is* a provider+model choice and exactly one validating constructor that produces it.
- **Retracted: "media slots may borrow the main connection."** Owner directive: a media slot (vision/transcribe) the user never configured is **disabled** — a clean error naming the slot, zero fallback to the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire. Silent defaults here are a credential-leak channel (see Security), not a convenience.
- **Retracted: "CLI problem."** The Flutter app reproduces the same selection logic through `AgentService` (incl. the media-slot fallback-to-main at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`). The binding logic lives in core `lib/`; both hosts are thin UI over it. Behavior — selection, restore, validation, error text — is byte-identical across hosts.

## Architecture

```
                entry points (ALL produce a binding or throw)
 ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
 │ FA_PROVIDER_* env │ CLI flags │ /model /provider │ session restore │ provider queue │ media slots │ Flutter settings │
 └────┴─────────┴──────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴─────┘
                                   │
                    ProviderModelBinding.resolve(...)   ← core lib/, ONLY constructor
                                   │  validates: wire kind ⇄ endpoint dialect,
                                   │  model ⇄ endpoint catalog, key slot ⇄ endpoint
                                   ▼
        ProviderModelBinding { recordName, providerKind(wire), baseUrl,
                               modelId, keyEnvRef, provenance }
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                              ▼
  session runtime          persisted state (record NAME,      both hosts render
  (roles, queue,           never kind-only)                   identical errors
   media, restore)
```

**Named components**

- **`ProviderModelBinding`** (core `lib/`, new): immutable value object — the complete identity of one provider+model choice: catalog record name (or explicit custom-record id), wire kind, normalized `baseUrl`, `modelId`, key env indirection (never a key value), and provenance (`env` / `flag` / `restore` / `command` / `queue` / `media` / `app`). Single validating constructor `ProviderModelBinding.resolve`; no other code path may construct one.
- **Binding validation rules** (all enforced inside `resolve`, all produce errors naming BOTH the model and the provider/endpoint):
  1. *Wire⇄endpoint*: the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind. An explicit override (e.g. `wire:` key in `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` / config record) is the only escape hatch and is echoed in every report.
  2. *Model⇄endpoint*: a model id is validated against the endpoint's model list when one is available. When the endpoint exposes no list, manual entry is ALWAYS allowed (decided, Q2): the prompt says `enter the model id manually — sent as-is`, the confirmation names the endpoint, and the status bar carries an `unverified` marker until the endpoint confirms the id; headless/non-TTY requires an explicit opt-in flag (`--allow-unverified`) so automation never blocks on a prompt.
  3. *Key⇄endpoint*: the key env indirection is resolved against the binding's own record, with normalized endpoint comparison (`sameEndpoint` semantics, as roles/key_status already use) deciding "custom endpoint" — never a raw string compare.
  4. *No partial overrides*: an entry point that changes only `model` (e.g. `--model` without `--provider`) revalidates the model against the *current* binding and rejects on mismatch; it never silently inherits provider/baseUrl from a different source.
- **BindingStore** (core `lib/`): persists the **record name** (or full custom record) + modelId + normalized baseUrl — never `providerKind` alone. Restart re-resolves the record, so kimi/codemie (which share wire kind `openai-completions`) restore their own catalog env names and endpoints.
- **Host parity layer**: CLI/TUI commands and the Flutter app (`AgentService`, settings UI) call the same `resolve`/`BindingStore` API. `flutter_app/` contains zero binding logic of its own; the shared test suite runs the same scenarios through both hosts.

**Invariants**

- I1: Every session's effective model comes from exactly one `ProviderModelBinding`; no code reads `model` and `provider` from different sources.
- I2: A binding that fails validation never reaches the network layer; the error names model, endpoint, and wire kind.
- I3: A media slot without explicit user configuration is **disabled**; vision/transcribe requests never contain the main provider's key, endpoint, or wire adapter.
- I4: A key resolved for endpoint E is never sent to an endpoint ≠ E (normalized comparison).
- I5: Persisted state round-trips: boot after restart yields a binding equal to the pre-shutdown one, for catalog and custom records alike.
- I6: TUI and Flutter app produce identical bindings and identical error text for identical inputs.

2. **Env preconfig**: add `wire` key support to `_supportedConfigKeys`; validate wire⇄endpoint dialect (the incident: FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic + OpenAI-compatible baseUrl). How do we know a baseUrl is "OpenAI-compatible"? We can't in general — but the ticket says "the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind". Known dialect = if the baseUrl matches a known catalog provider's default endpoint for a DIFFERENT dialect, it's a mismatch. E.g. baseUrl `https://api.z.ai/...` known zai dialect vs wire anthropic → mismatch. The incident: LAN OpenAI proxy — how would we know it's OpenAI-compatible? Hmm, in the incident, `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` model id — the model prefix names the provider `zai`! Model ids with `provider/model` prefix form: `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`, `anthropic/claude-...`, `openai/gpt-...`. OpenRouter-style ids. So model⇄endpoint validation can catch `zai/glm-5.3-flashx` on a wire=anthropic binding: the model id's catalog family is zai (openai-completions wire), mismatching the anthropic wire.

Also baseUrl host matching: if baseUrl host matches a catalog spec's default endpoint host (e.g. api.anthropic.com) but wire kind is openai-completions → mismatch.

So validation rules for wire⇄endpoint:
- if baseUrl matches (normalized/sameEndpoint) any catalog spec's defaultBaseUrl with a different kind → error.
- if modelId has a `<family>/` prefix where family resolves to a catalog spec with a known kind different from the wire kind → error.

1. The model id carries a `vendor/` prefix that resolves to a catalog provider (openrouter-style ids like `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`, `anthropic/claude-...`).
2. The baseUrl matches a known catalog endpoint of a different wire kind.

There's no static authoritative model⇄provider catalog — model list knowledge comes from the endpoint (`/models`) with `_knownModels` + `remoteCatalogEnrichment` as last-resort fallbacks. So "Model⇄endpoint" validation can only be definitively enforced when:
1. The model id carries a `vendor/` prefix that resolves to a catalog provider (openrouter-style ids like `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`, `anthropic/claude-...`).
2. The baseUrl matches a known catalog endpoint of a different wire kind.

That's exactly the incident (H1/AC2): `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + OpenAI-compatible proxy baseUrl + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`. The `zai/` prefix → zai catalog spec kind `zai` ≠ `anthropic` wire → reject. The `wire:` override is the escape hatch.

For AC3 (--model gpt-5 over saved anthropic): `gpt-5` has no vendor prefix... how to detect? Hmm. The gpt family prefix `gpt-` maps to openai wire. We could add a small heuristic table of well-known model-family prefixes → wire kind (gpt-*/o3*/o4* → openai-completions; claude-* → anthropic; gemini-* → google; glm-* → zai/openai; kimi/k3/kimi-* → openai-completions...). That's the "declared/known dialect" idea. The ticket says "the endpoint's declared/known dialect must match the wire kind". For the --model mismatch we need known-dialect knowledge for the MODEL id. A conservative `modelWireHint(modelId)` returning a known wire kind for well-known families (claude → anthropic, gemini → google, gpt-/o1-/o3-/o4- → openai) and null when unknown. Validation rejects only on a KNOWN conflict; unknown ids pass (with the `unverified` marker per D2 when no list exists — that part is TUI flow).

### 1. New core: `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`
Pure Dart (no dart:io). Contains:

```dart
enum BindingProvenance { env, flag, restore, command, queue, media, app }

final class ProviderModelBinding {
  final String? recordName;      // catalog record name or custom entry name
  final String providerKind;     // wire kind
  final String baseUrl;          // normalized (no trailing slash)
  final String modelId;
  final String? keyEnvRef;       // env indirection (never a value)
  final BindingProvenance provenance;
  final String? wireOverride;    // the explicit `wire:` escape hatch value; echoed in reports

  static ProviderModelBinding resolve({required String providerKind, required String modelId, String? baseUrl, String? recordName, String? keyEnvRef, required BindingProvenance provenance, String? wireOverride, Iterable<ProviderSpec> catalog = providerCatalog.values});

```

Validation in `resolve`:
- modelId shape (E5): reject empty, whitespace, control chars, URL-ish (`://`, scheme), length cap.
- baseUrl normalization (strip trailing slash).
- wire⇄endpoint: baseUrl matching another catalog spec's default endpoint (sameEndpoint) whose kind differs → error naming model, endpoint, wire kind, unless wireOverride == providerKind (echoed). Also model family prefix `vendor/` resolving via catalog → kind mismatch → error; also known model family heuristic (claude → anthropic, gemini → google, gpt → openai-completions...) → mismatch → error.
- `wireOverride` present but not equal to providerKind → error? Or the override CHANGES the wire? The ticket: "An explicit override (e.g. `wire:` key in FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / config record) is the only escape hatch and is echoed in every report." So `wire:` names the wire kind to actually use (overriding the type-mapped spec kind). I'll implement: when `wire` is declared in env config, the binding's providerKind becomes the declared wire, validated to be a known adapter kind, and `wireOverride` records that it was declared (echoed in reports). If declared wire is not a known kind → ConfigException.

Also `BindingReport`/`describe()` returning the echo string: `record "kimi" (wire openai-completions) @ https://api.kimi.example/v1 model kimi-k2 (provenance: env; wire override: openai-completions)`.

Errors: a dedicated `BindingException`? Repo has `ConfigException` in lib/src/exceptions.dart — use that (boot maps it to fa: usage failure). Errors must name model, endpoint, wire kind (I2).

/// The ONE validated provider+model identity (gh-1570)...

enum BindingProvenance { env, flag, restore, command, queue, media, app }

final class ProviderModelBinding {
  final String? recordName;

  final String modelId;
  final String? keyEnvRef;
  final BindingProvenance provenance;
  final bool wireOverride;
}
```

resolve parameters:
```dart
factory ProviderModelBinding.resolve({
  required String providerKind,
  required String modelId,
  String? baseUrl,
  String? recordName,
  String? keyEnvRef,
  required BindingProvenance provenance,

  bool honorBuildFilter = false, // hmm — the catalog scan should be filter-less like resolveCliProviderSpec default (restore path); queue/CLI surfaces could pass true. Keep filter-less (the boot restore stance) for determinism.
})

Validation steps:
1. `wire` declared → resolveCliProviderSpec(wire) must be non-null → kind = resolved spec kind? No — wire names an ADAPTER kind; validate it's a known kind by scanning providerCatalog kinds. `providerKind = wire` (normalized lowercase). wireOverride = true.
2. baseUrl: null/blank → if the kind resolves to exactly ONE catalog entry → spec.defaultBaseUrl; if shared kind (openai-completions) → ConfigException "provider '<kind>' is an endpoint-shared wire — declare baseUrl". (For queue entries this kills M5: openai-completions without baseUrl → error.)
3. normalizeBaseUrl: trim; strip ONE trailing slash.
4. modelId shape validation (E5): non-empty after trim; no whitespace; no control chars; no '://' ; length ≤ 200; must not start with '-' ... keep: allowed pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9._:@/+-]*[A-Za-z0-9._+])?$` — hmm, model ids like `openai/gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-4.1-mini`, `kimi-for-coding-highspeed`, `@cf/...`? `SessionContext.model` comes from the last `model_change` record OR assistant message. An assistant-message-derived model carries no baseUrl/customProvider. The leaf model from a `model_change` record is authoritative; from an assistant message it's the model that generated the last message, which is also the effective model actually... Actually the safest approach aligned with the ticket: apply the leaf binding when the leaf provider kind differs from the current provider kind OR the model id differs, whenever the leaf provider resolves through the catalog — i.e., always apply when resolvable. The guard `baseUrl != null || customProvider != null` was there presumably to avoid switching when the leaf record doesn't pin an endpoint (avoid wrongly re-pointing a custom-endpoint session onto a default endpoint). Applying provider+model without baseUrl means: use the spec's default endpoint. But if the session actually ran on a custom endpoint with a pre-gh-1000 record that had no baseUrl... the restore would silently move it to the default endpoint. Hmm. But that risk is exactly what the ticket accepts: for default-endpoint providers the leaf must be applied.

The refined fix honoring both concerns: apply the leaf when the leaf's provider RESOLVES to a spec AND (the leaf pins baseUrl/customProvider OR the leaf's provider kind's default endpoint would be used — i.e., we only skip when applying would DOWNGRADE an endpoint-pinned session to default). Since a leaf without baseUrl/customProvider carries no endpoint info, applying provider+modelId means binding to the spec's default endpoint. The ticket explicitly wants that for default-endpoint providers (anthropic/google/zai leaves have baseUrl == null).

So the change: in step 1, apply the leaf whenever `resolveCliProviderSpec(leafModel.provider) != null` AND the leaf provider kind is NOT the ambiguous `openai-completions` kind without endpoint info (for that kind, keep the folder-state fallback). For unambiguous providers (anthropic, google, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, chatgpt, kimi, codemie, openrouter as names...), apply.

So the M4 fix in step 1: apply the leaf binding when the spec resolves and (baseUrl != null || customProvider != null || spec.kind is endpoint-unambiguous). But careful: anthropic-kind model could be served via a custom proxy baseUrl — with no pin we can't know. The ticket accepts binding to the default endpoint in that case? If the session ran on a proxy, the model_change record from the switch would have pinned baseUrl (since gh-1000). Legacy pre-gh-1000 sessions on proxies are edge; the ticket prioritizes the claude-on-copilot failure.

On the anthropic WIRE, a `vendor/model` id would be sent to anthropic endpoint — anthropic wire never carries vendor-prefixed ids legitimately. So the rule can be wire-specific: vendor-prefixed ids are an OpenAI-completions-ecosystem convention (openrouter-style). A binding whose wire is NOT openai-completions and whose model id carries a vendor prefix of a KNOWN catalog provider → mismatch (the prefix names a provider whose wire differs; non-openai wires don't route vendor ids). More precisely: prefix resolves to spec X; if X.kind != providerKind AND providerKind != 'openai-completions'... no wait: binding openai-completions + `anthropic/claude-...` on openrouter = legit (prefix kind anthropic != openai-completions, but the endpoint openrouter routes it). Vendor prefix on a NON-openai-completions binding (anthropic/google/zai/minimax/copilot/dial/chatgpt-codex) = mismatch → error naming both sides + hint.

final class ProviderModelBinding {

resolve parameters:
```dart
factory ProviderModelBinding.resolve({
  required String providerKind,
  required String modelId,
  String? baseUrl,
  String? recordName,

  bool honorBuildFilter = false, // hmm — the catalog scan should be filter-less like resolveCliProviderSpec default (restore path); queue/CLI surfaces could pass true. Keep filter-less (the boot restore stance) for determinism.

Validation steps:
1. `wire` declared → resolveCliProviderSpec(wire) must be non-null → kind = resolved spec kind? No — wire names an ADAPTER kind; validate it's a known kind by scanning providerCatalog kinds. `providerKind = wire` (normalized lowercase). wireOverride = true.

3. normalizeBaseUrl: trim; strip ONE trailing slash.

3. normalizeBaseUrl: trim; strip ONE trailing slash.
4. modelId shape validation (E5): non-empty after trim; no whitespace; no control chars; no '://' ; length ≤ 200; must not start with '-' ... keep: allowed pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9._:@/+-]*[A-Za-z0-9._+])?$` — hmm, model ids like `openai/gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-4.1-mini`, `kimi-for-coding-highspeed`, `@cf/...`? On the anthropic WIRE, a `vendor/model` id would be sent to anthropic endpoint — anthropic wire never carries vendor-prefixed ids legitimately. So the rule can be wire-specific: vendor-prefixed ids are an OpenAI-completions-ecosystem convention (openrouter-style). A binding whose wire is NOT openai-completions and whose model id carries a vendor prefix of a KNOWN catalog provider → mismatch (the prefix names a provider whose wire differs; non-openai wires don't route vendor ids). More precisely: prefix resolves to spec X; if X.kind != providerKind AND providerKind != 'openai-completions'... no wait: binding openai-completions + `anthropic/claude-...` on openrouter = legit (prefix kind anthropic != openai-completions, but the endpoint openrouter routes it). Vendor prefix on a NON-openai-completions binding (anthropic/google/zai/minimax/copilot/dial/chatgpt-codex) = mismatch → error naming both sides + hint.

resolve parameters:

factory ProviderModelBinding.resolve({
  required String providerKind,

Validation steps:

2. baseUrl: null/blank → if the kind resolves to exactly ONE catalog entry → spec.defaultBaseUrl; if shared kind (openai-completions) → ConfigException "provider '<kind>' is an endpoint-shared wire — declare baseUrl". (For queue entries this kills M5: openai-completions without baseUrl → error.)
3. normalizeBaseUrl: trim; strip ONE trailing slash.
4. modelId shape validation (E5): non-empty after trim; no whitespace; no control chars; no '://' ; length ≤ 200; must not start with '-' ... keep: allowed pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9._:@/+-]*[A-Za-z0-9._+])?$` — hmm, model ids like `openai/gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-4.1-mini`, `kimi-for-coding-highspeed`, `@cf/...`? 5. Wire⇄endpoint: scan catalog for a spec whose defaultBaseUrl sameEndpoint-matches baseUrl with kind != providerKind → error naming model, endpoint, wire kind, expected wire (the matched spec's kind) + hint "declare wire: <expected> only when the endpoint genuinely speaks <wire>".
   - Note: multiple catalog entries share defaultBaseUrl? Check: openrouter https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, kimi https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1, openai https://api.openai.com/v1, chatgpt chatGptCodexBaseUrl, copilot copilotIndividualBaseUrl, codemie defaultCodeMieBaseUrl/code-assistant-api/v1, dial ai-proxy.lab.epam.com, minimax api.minimax.io/v1, anthropic api.anthropic.com, google generativelanguage, zai api.z.ai/..., aiin. Probably unique enough.

A binding whose wire is NOT openai-completions and whose model id carries a vendor prefix of a KNOWN catalog provider → mismatch (the prefix names a provider whose wire differs; non-openai wires don't route vendor ids). Vendor prefix on a NON-openai-completions binding (anthropic/google/zai/minimax/copilot/dial/chatgpt-codex) = mismatch → error naming both sides + hint.

/// The ONE validated provider+model identity (gh-1570)...

enum BindingProvenance { env, flag, restore, command, queue, media, app }

final class ProviderModelBinding {
  final String? recordName;

  final String modelId;

}
```

resolve parameters:
```dart
factory ProviderModelBinding.resolve({
  required String providerKind,
  required String modelId,
  String? baseUrl,
  String? recordName,
  String? keyEnvRef,
  required BindingProvenance provenance,
  String? wire,
  bool honorBuildFilter = false, // hmm — the catalog scan should be filter-less like resolveCliProviderSpec default (restore path); queue/CLI surfaces could pass true. Keep filter-less (the boot restore stance) for determinism.
})

Validation steps:
1. `wire` declared → resolveCliProviderSpec(wire) must be non-null → kind = resolved spec kind? No — wire names an ADAPTER kind; validate it's a known kind by scanning providerCatalog kinds. `providerKind = wire` (normalized lowercase). wireOverride = true.

3. normalizeBaseUrl: trim; strip ONE trailing slash.
4. modelId shape validation (E5): non-empty after trim; no whitespace; no control chars; no '://' ; length ≤ 200; must not start with '-' ... keep: allowed pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9._:@/+-]*[A-Za-z0-9._+])?$` — hmm, model ids like `openai/gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-4.1-mini`, `kimi-for-coding-highspeed`, `@cf/...`? 5. Wire⇄endpoint: scan catalog for a spec whose defaultBaseUrl sameEndpoint-matches baseUrl with kind != providerKind → error naming model, endpoint, wire kind, expected wire (the matched spec's kind) + hint "declare wire: <expected> only when the endpoint genuinely speaks <wire>".
   - Note: multiple catalog entries share defaultBaseUrl? Check: openrouter https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, kimi https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1, openai https://api.openai.com/v1, chatgpt chatGptCodexBaseUrl, copilot copilotIndividualBaseUrl, codemie defaultCodeMieBaseUrl/code-assistant-api/v1, dial ai-proxy.lab.epam.com, minimax api.minimax.io/v1, anthropic api.anthropic.com, google generativelanguage, zai api.z.ai/..., aiin. A binding whose wire is NOT openai-completions and whose model id carries a vendor prefix of a KNOWN catalog provider → mismatch (the prefix names a provider whose wire differs; non-openai wires don't route vendor ids).
