blocks.text:
The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓
- openai-completions-kind binding @ codex endpoint: which spec? resolveCliProviderSpec('openai-completions', baseUrl: codex-url) → legacy rule: baseUrl != null → openai spec. api openai-completions vs spec(chatgpt).api responses → reject ✓

For the vendor-prefix rule (`zai/glm-...` on non-openai wire): compare prefix spec's API vs binding spec's API — `anthropic` binding + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`: anthropic-messages vs zai's openai-completions → reject ✓. And `openai/gpt-4o` on anthropic binding: openai api openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (good — that's also a real mismatch class). On openai-completions binding: equal apis → pass ✓. My current rule exempted openai-completions-bound wires entirely; comparing apis generalizes correctly: openrouter binding + `anthropic/claude-...` → apis equal (both openai-completions) → pass ✓.

For the model-family hint on a known endpoint: hint must map to an API DIALECT. Hints: claude → anthropic-messages; gemini → google-generative-ai; gpt/o1/o3/o4/chatgpt → openai-completions. Compare hint dialect vs endpoint-owning spec's api:
- gpt-5 + api.anthropic.com: openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (H2)
- claude-sonnet + api.openai.com: anthropic-messages vs openai-completions → reject. Hmm — is that a false positive? claude models via an OPENAI-compatible... api.openai.com does NOT serve claude models. Rejecting is correct!
- gemini-2.5-pro + openrouter endpoint: google-generative-ai vs openai-completions → REJECT. But `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` (prefixed) works on openrouter; BARE `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter? OpenRouter's ids are prefixed (`google/gemini-2.5-pro`) — bare `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter would 400. Hmm — but wait: my `_knownModels['openrouter']` list includes 'google/gemini-2.5-pro' (prefixed). Bare gemini on openrouter: unlikely to work. BUT — glm-... hmm no. What about copilot? Copilot serves claude/gpt models BARE over openai-completions wire (GitHub Models / Copilot API serves `claude-sonnet-4` etc.)! Copilot spec api is 'openai-completions', endpoint api.githubcopilot.com. A copilot binding + `claude-sonnet-4-5` (a REAL copilot model id!) → hint anthropic-messages vs copilot's openai-completions → FALSE POSITIVE — would break legit copilot usage. Damn.

Let me check the copilot model ids... The `_visionModel` mentions copilot; copilot models in the wild are like `claude-sonnet-4` — yes, bare claude ids are Copilot's model naming. Also the kimi coding endpoint serves `kimi-for-coding`... and DIAL deployments can be named anything (`anthropic/claude-...`? DIAL deployment names like `claude-...`? EPAM DIAL deployments are typically `gpt-4o`, `claude-...`-ish names too!).

So the bare-family rule is ONLY safe against endpoints that provably don't serve other families: api.anthropic.com serves ONLY claude models; api.openai.com serves ONLY gpt models; generativelanguage serves ONLY gemini. So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + gpt-5 → REJECT ✓ (H2!)
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + claude-* → pass
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + gemini-2.5-pro → REJECT ✓
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + claude-sonnet → REJECT — hmm, is api.openai.com ever a proxy for claude? No — OpenAI's own API. Correct to reject... unless a user points --base-url at api.openai.com running some gateway? They'd be reimplementing api.openai.com. Accept.
- endpoint openrouter/copilot/kimi/zai/dial/LAN → NO bare-family check (multi-family routers) → pass ✓ (copilot claude ids safe, DIAL safe).

So implement: `_canonicalFamilyDialect(endpoint)` → returns the family-dialect ONLY for the three single-family canonical endpoints (anthropic/openai/google specs where spec.name == the family owner). Better: a static map of canonical endpoints → their family wire-dialect: use the spec where the endpoint is the default AND the spec is the FAMILY OWNER (anthropic spec → anthropic-messages family; openai spec → openai-completions family; google spec → google-generative-ai family). Then reject when modelId's hint dialect != that family dialect. This keeps copilot (kind copilot, api openai-completions — but NOT the openai FAMILY owner) exempt. Wait — copilot's api IS openai-completions but its endpoint isn't api.openai.com so it's exempt from the bare check anyway. And wire⇄endpoint via api comparison for copilot: copilot binding @ api.openai.com? copilot api openai-completions == openai api → pass — hmm, copilot wire @ openai endpoint would actually need the copilot token exchange — but dialect-wise the wire is openai-completions-compatible. Now the wire⇄endpoint api-comparison rule: binding spec api vs endpoint-owning spec X api. Binding kind 'openai-completions' @ dial endpoint: legacy rule resolves openai spec, api openai-completions == dial api → pass. Correct (dial speaks openai-completions; DIAL needs the Api-Key header + path rewrite, handled by the dial adapter via kind — a plain openai binding @ dial endpoint would actually fail on auth/path... but dialect-wise passable; the binding layer is about wire dialect, fine).

zai endpoint + binding kind 'zai' → same spec → pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'kimi' → same spec pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'codemie'? codemie api openai-completions == kimi api → pass (dialect-compatible, endpoint/key layer sorts the rest). OK.

resolve parameters:

factory ProviderModelBinding.resolve({
  required String providerKind,

Validation steps:

3. normalizeBaseUrl: trim; strip ONE trailing slash.

So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + gpt-5 → REJECT ✓ (H2!)
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + claude-* → pass
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + gemini-2.5-pro → REJECT ✓
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + claude-sonnet → REJECT — hmm, is api.openai.com ever a proxy for claude? No — OpenAI's own API. Correct to reject... unless a user points --base-url at api.openai.com running some gateway? They'd be reimplementing api.openai.com. Accept.
- endpoint openrouter/copilot/kimi/zai/dial/LAN → NO bare-family check (multi-family routers) → pass ✓ (copilot claude ids safe, DIAL safe).

So implement: `_canonicalFamilyDialect(endpoint)` → returns the family-dialect ONLY for the three single-family canonical endpoints (anthropic/openai/google specs where spec.name == the family owner). Better: a static map of canonical endpoints → their family wire-dialect: use the spec where the endpoint is the default AND the spec is the FAMILY OWNER (anthropic spec → anthropic-messages family; openai spec → openai-completions family; google spec → google-generative-ai family). Then reject when modelId's hint dialect != that family dialect. This keeps copilot (kind copilot, api openai-completions — but NOT the openai FAMILY owner) exempt. Wait — copilot's api IS openai-completions but its endpoint isn't api.openai.com so it's exempt from the bare check anyway. And wire⇄endpoint via api comparison for copilot: copilot binding @ api.openai.com? copilot api openai-completions == openai api → pass — hmm, copilot wire @ openai endpoint would actually need the copilot token exchange — but dialect-wise the wire is openai-completions-compatible. Binding kind 'openai-completions' @ dial endpoint: legacy rule resolves openai spec, api openai-completions == dial api → pass. Correct (dial speaks openai-completions; DIAL needs the Api-Key header + path rewrite, handled by the dial adapter via kind — a plain openai binding @ dial endpoint would actually fail on auth/path... but dialect-wise passable; the binding layer is about wire dialect, fine).

12:/// provider config). What it validates:
13:///
14:/// 1. *Wire ⇄ endpoint* — the endpoint's declared/known dialect must
15:///    match the wire kind. A known endpoint of ANOTHER dialect
16:///    ([ProviderSpec.defaultBaseUrl], [sameEndpoint]-normalized) and a
17:///    vendor-prefixed model id (`zai/glm-…`) riding a non-openai wire are
18:///    both rejections. An explicit `wire:` override is the only escape
19:///    hatch and is echoed in every report (E6: a genuinely
20:///    foreign-dialect endpoint behind a custom baseUrl passes only
21:///    through it).

27:///    (D2: the `unverified` marker territory, never a silent guess).

messages.preview: The `api` field is the true dialect. Let me fix the validators to compare API dialects (keeps the bench's `openai @ zai-endpoint` config valid, still catches the incident class):

blocks.text:
The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓
- openai-completions-kind binding @ codex endpoint: which spec? resolveCliProviderSpec('openai-completions', baseUrl: codex-url) → legacy rule: baseUrl != null → openai spec. api openai-completions vs spec(chatgpt).api responses → reject ✓

For the vendor-prefix rule (`zai/glm-...` on non-openai wire): compare prefix spec's API vs binding spec's API — `anthropic` binding + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`: anthropic-messages vs zai's openai-completions → reject ✓. And `openai/gpt-4o` on anthropic binding: openai api openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (good — that's also a real mismatch class). On openai-completions binding: equal apis → pass ✓. My current rule exempted openai-completions-bound wires entirely; comparing apis generalizes correctly: openrouter binding + `anthropic/claude-...` → apis equal (both openai-completions) → pass ✓.

For the model-family hint on a known endpoint: hint must map to an API DIALECT. Hints: claude → anthropic-messages; gemini → google-generative-ai; gpt/o1/o3/o4/chatgpt → openai-completions. Compare hint dialect vs endpoint-owning spec's api:
- gpt-5 + api.anthropic.com: openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (H2)
- claude-sonnet + api.openai.com: anthropic-messages vs openai-completions → reject. Hmm — is that a false positive? claude models via an OPENAI-compatible... api.openai.com does NOT serve claude models. Rejecting is correct!
- gemini-2.5-pro + openrouter endpoint: google-generative-ai vs openai-completions → REJECT. But `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` (prefixed) works on openrouter; BARE `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter? OpenRouter's ids are prefixed (`google/gemini-2.5-pro`) — bare `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter would 400. Hmm — but wait: my `_knownModels['openrouter']` list includes 'google/gemini-2.5-pro' (prefixed). Bare gemini on openrouter: unlikely to work. BUT — glm-... hmm no. What about copilot? Copilot serves claude/gpt models BARE over openai-completions wire (GitHub Models / Copilot API serves `claude-sonnet-4` etc.)! Copilot spec api is 'openai-completions', endpoint api.githubcopilot.com. A copilot binding + `claude-sonnet-4-5` (a REAL copilot model id!) → hint anthropic-messages vs copilot's openai-completions → FALSE POSITIVE — would break legit copilot usage. Damn.

Let me check the copilot model ids... The `_visionModel` mentions copilot; copilot models in the wild are like `claude-sonnet-4` — yes, bare claude ids are Copilot's model naming. Also the kimi coding endpoint serves `kimi-for-coding`... and DIAL deployments can be named anything (`anthropic/claude-...`? DIAL deployment names like `claude-...`? EPAM DIAL deployments are typically `gpt-4o`, `claude-...`-ish names too!).

So the bare-family rule is ONLY safe against endpoints that provably don't serve other families: api.anthropic.com serves ONLY claude models; api.openai.com serves ONLY gpt models; generativelanguage serves ONLY gemini. So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + gpt-5 → REJECT ✓ (H2!)
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + claude-* → pass
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + gemini-2.5-pro → REJECT ✓
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + claude-sonnet → REJECT — hmm, is api.openai.com ever a proxy for claude? No — OpenAI's own API. Correct to reject... unless a user points --base-url at api.openai.com running some gateway? They'd be reimplementing api.openai.com. Accept.
- endpoint openrouter/copilot/kimi/zai/dial/LAN → NO bare-family check (multi-family routers) → pass ✓ (copilot claude ids safe, DIAL safe).

So implement: `_canonicalFamilyDialect(endpoint)` → returns the family-dialect ONLY for the three single-family canonical endpoints (anthropic/openai/google specs where spec.name == the family owner). Better: a static map of canonical endpoints → their family wire-dialect: use the spec where the endpoint is the default AND the spec is the FAMILY OWNER (anthropic spec → anthropic-messages family; openai spec → openai-completions family; google spec → google-generative-ai family). Then reject when modelId's hint dialect != that family dialect. This keeps copilot (kind copilot, api openai-completions — but NOT the openai FAMILY owner) exempt. Wait — copilot's api IS openai-completions but its endpoint isn't api.openai.com so it's exempt from the bare check anyway. And wire⇄endpoint via api comparison for copilot: copilot binding @ api.openai.com? copilot api openai-completions == openai api → pass — hmm, copilot wire @ openai endpoint would actually need the copilot token exchange — but dialect-wise the wire is openai-completions-compatible. The endpoint-LOCKED check in startup already refuses copilot over foreign endpoints (endpointLocked). Fine.

Now the wire⇄endpoint api-comparison rule: binding spec api vs endpoint-owning spec X api. One more false-positive check: dial endpoint (ai-proxy.lab.epam.com, api openai-completions) + binding kind 'dial' → same spec → pass. Binding kind 'openai-completions' @ dial endpoint: legacy rule resolves openai spec, api openai-completions == dial api → pass. Correct (dial speaks openai-completions; DIAL needs the Api-Key header + path rewrite, handled by the dial adapter via kind — a plain openai binding @ dial endpoint would actually fail on auth/path... but dialect-wise passable; the binding layer is about wire dialect, fine).

zai endpoint + binding kind 'zai' → same spec → pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'kimi' → same spec pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'codemie'? codemie api openai-completions == kimi api → pass (dialect-compatible, endpoint/key layer sorts the rest). OK.

Let me now rewrite those two validators in the binding module and update my tests:
- Test 'a known endpoint of another dialect is rejected': anthropic @ api.openai.com → apis anthropic-messages vs openai-completions → reject ✓ (message must contain api.openai.com + anthropic).
- Test 'trailing-slash spelling of a foreign endpoint' (zai endpoint, trailing slash): anthropic binding @ zai endpoint → apis differ → reject ✓.
- Test 'gemini-2.5-pro on openrouter rejected' — I need to REVERSE this: openrouter is a multi-family router → bare gemini PASSES now. Update my test to expect PASS (and add a canonical-endpoint rejection test: gemini-2.5-pro @ api.openai.com/v1 → reject).
- The vendor-prefix test stays (zai/ on anthropic binding rejected via api mismatch).

Also update the binding doc comments to reflect api-dialect semantics.

1:/// The ONE validated provider+model identity (gh-1570): every way a
2:/// session picks its model — env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`,
3:/// `/provider`, session restore, the provider queue, media slots, the
4:/// Flutter app settings — produces a [ProviderModelBinding] through
5:/// [ProviderModelBinding.resolve] or fails with an error naming BOTH
6:/// sides. A model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire
7:/// format, or API key.
8:///
9:/// The binding is the boundary INTO the already-correct resolved world
10:/// (`ModelRef.parse` requires a provider, `ModelRolesResolver` assembles
11:/// model+key+stream from one ref, `ProviderQueueEntry` carries its own
12:/// provider config). What it validates:
13:///
14:/// 1. *Wire ⇄ endpoint* — the endpoint's declared/known dialect must
15:///    match the wire kind. A known endpoint of ANOTHER dialect
16:///    ([ProviderSpec.defaultBaseUrl], [sameEndpoint]-normalized) and a
17:///    vendor-prefixed model id (`zai/glm-…`) riding a non-openai wire are
18:///    both rejections. An explicit `wire:` override is the only escape
19:///    hatch and is echoed in every report (E6: a genuinely
20:///    foreign-dialect endpoint behind a custom baseUrl passes only
21:///    through it).
22:/// 2. *Model ⇄ endpoint* — a model id whose family is KNOWN
23:///    ([modelFamilyWireHint]: `claude-*` is anthropic wire, `gemini-*`
24:///    google, `gpt-*`/`o1`/`o3`/`o4-*` openai-completions) is rejected on
25:///    a KNOWN endpoint of another dialect. Unknown ids and unknown
26:///    endpoints always pass — there is nothing to check them against
27:///    (D2: the `unverified` marker territory, never a silent guess).
28:/// 3. *Endpoint-shared wires* — `openai-completions` is six catalog
29:///    records (openai, openrouter, kimi, codemie, …). A binding on that
30:///    wire with NO record name and NO baseUrl has no identity at all and
31:///    is rejected instead of silently riding the legacy openrouter
32:///    default (M5: `OPENAI_API_KEY` sent to openrouter.ai).
33:/// 4. *Id shape and key indirection* — a model id carrying URL-ish or
34:///    control content is rejected before any endpoint call (E5); a key
35:///    ref must be an environment-variable NAME — key VALUES never enter
36:///    a binding (S3).
37:///
38:/// Pure Dart: no `dart:io`, no network — validation uses the provider
39:/// catalog only.

47:enum BindingProvenance {
48:  env,

52:  queue,
53:  media,
54:  app;

56:  /// The label reports render.

58:    BindingProvenance.env => 'env',

68:/// The complete identity of one provider+model choice: the catalog
69:/// record (or custom entry) name, the wire kind, the normalized endpoint,
70:/// the model id, the key's env indirection, and the provenance.
71:///
72:/// Construct ONLY through [ProviderModelBinding.resolve] — the single
73:/// validating constructor. Every field is immutable; equality covers the
74:/// identity fields (record, wire, endpoint, model, key ref) so a
75:/// persisted state can round-trip (I5) regardless of which entry point

77:final class ProviderModelBinding {
78:  ProviderModelBinding._({
79:    required this.recordName,
80:    required this.providerKind,
81:    required this.baseUrl,
82:    required this.modelId,
83:    required this.keyEnvRef,
84:    required this.provenance,
85:    required this.wireOverride,
86:  });
87:
88:  /// Resolves and VALIDATES one provider+model choice.
89:  ///
90:  /// [providerKind] is the caller's provider identity — a catalog name
91:  /// (`kimi`), an adapter kind (`anthropic`), or the shared
92:  /// `openai-completions` kind. [recordName] names the specific catalog
93:  /// or saved custom record when the caller knows it (endpoint-shared
94:  /// wires NEED it or an explicit [baseUrl]). [baseUrl] overrides the
95:  /// record's default endpoint; it is normalized (one trailing slash
96:  /// stripped). [wire] is the explicit `wire:` escape hatch: the declared
97:  /// adapter kind REPLACES the record's own wire kind and silences the
98:  /// dialect checks (the caller asserted the endpoint speaks it); the
99:  /// override is echoed by [echo]. [keyEnvRef] is the key's environment
100:  /// indirection — a NAME, never a value.
101:  ///
102:  /// Throws [ConfigException] naming the model, the endpoint, and the
103:  /// wire kind on every validation failure (I2).
104:  factory ProviderModelBinding.resolve({
105:    required String providerKind,
106:    required String modelId,
107:    String? baseUrl,
108:    String? recordName,
109:    String? keyEnvRef,
110:    BindingProvenance provenance = BindingProvenance.command,
111:    String? wire,
112:  }) {
113:    final name = recordName?.trim() ?? '';
114:    final rawKind = providerKind.trim().toLowerCase();
115:    if (rawKind.isEmpty) {
116:      throw const ConfigException(
117:        'provider model binding: no provider given — name the provider '
118:        'record (or adapter kind) the model rides',
119:      );
120:    }
121:    validateModelIdShape(modelId);
122:
123:    // The `wire:` escape hatch resolves FIRST: it is the adapter kind the
124:    // caller asserts the endpoint speaks, validated against the known
125:    // adapter kinds so a typo fails loud instead of inventing a wire.
126:    String? declaredWire;
127:    if (wire != null && wire.trim().isNotEmpty) {
128:      final declared = wire.trim().toLowerCase();
129:      final known = providerCatalog.values.any((spec) => spec.kind == declared);
130:      if (!known) {
131:        throw ConfigException(
132:          'unknown wire kind "$declared" — supported wire kinds: '
133:          '${providerCatalog.values.map((s) => s.kind).toSet().join(', ')}',
134:        );
135:      }
136:      declaredWire = declared;
137:    }
138:
139:    // The record: a catalog name/kind resolves to its spec (the ONE
140:    // both-identifier lookup). An unknown id with no wire override is a
141:    // fail-loud rejection — a binding names a real record or it names
142:    // nothing.
143:    final spec = resolveCliProviderSpec(
144:      name.isNotEmpty ? name : rawKind,
145:      baseUrl: baseUrl,
146:    );
147:    if (spec == null) {
148:      throw ConfigException(
149:        'unknown provider record "$providerKind" — a model binding names a '
150:        'provider catalog record (or adapter kind)',
151:      );
152:    }
153:    final wireKind = declaredWire ?? spec.kind;
154:    final override = declaredWire != null && declaredWire != spec.kind;
155:
156:    // Endpoint: explicit, else the record's own default. The endpoint-
157:    // shared kind with neither is identity-less — reject instead of
158:    // silently riding the legacy openrouter default (M5).
159:    final effectiveBaseUrl = _resolveBaseUrl(
160:      baseUrl: baseUrl,
161:      spec: spec,
162:      name: name,
163:      rawKind: rawKind,

Let me check the copilot model ids... The `_visionModel` mentions copilot; copilot models in the wild are like `claude-sonnet-4` — yes, bare claude ids are Copilot's model naming. Also the kimi coding endpoint serves `kimi-for-coding`... and DIAL deployments can be named anything (`anthropic/claude-...`? DIAL deployment names like `claude-...`? EPAM DIAL deployments are typically `gpt-4o`, `claude-...`-ish names too!).

So the bare-family rule is ONLY safe against endpoints that provably don't serve other families: api.anthropic.com serves ONLY claude models; api.openai.com serves ONLY gpt models; generativelanguage serves ONLY gemini. So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + gpt-5 → REJECT ✓ (H2!)
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + claude-* → pass
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + gemini-2.5-pro → REJECT ✓
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + claude-sonnet → REJECT — hmm, is api.openai.com ever a proxy for claude? No — OpenAI's own API. Correct to reject... unless a user points --base-url at api.openai.com running some gateway? They'd be reimplementing api.openai.com. Accept.
- endpoint openrouter/copilot/kimi/zai/dial/LAN → NO bare-family check (multi-family routers) → pass ✓ (copilot claude ids safe, DIAL safe).

So implement: `_canonicalFamilyDialect(endpoint)` → returns the family-dialect ONLY for the three single-family canonical endpoints (anthropic/openai/google specs where spec.name == the family owner). Better: a static map of canonical endpoints → their family wire-dialect: use the spec where the endpoint is the default AND the spec is the FAMILY OWNER (anthropic spec → anthropic-messages family; openai spec → openai-completions family; google spec → google-generative-ai family). Then reject when modelId's hint dialect != that family dialect. This keeps copilot (kind copilot, api openai-completions — but NOT the openai FAMILY owner) exempt. Wait — copilot's api IS openai-completions but its endpoint isn't api.openai.com so it's exempt from the bare check anyway. And wire⇄endpoint via api comparison for copilot: copilot binding @ api.openai.com? copilot api openai-completions == openai api → pass — hmm, copilot wire @ openai endpoint would actually need the copilot token exchange — but dialect-wise the wire is openai-completions-compatible. The endpoint-LOCKED check in startup already refuses copilot over foreign endpoints (endpointLocked). Fine.

Binding kind 'openai-completions' @ dial endpoint: legacy rule resolves openai spec, api openai-completions == dial api → pass. Correct (dial speaks openai-completions; DIAL needs the Api-Key header + path rewrite, handled by the dial adapter via kind — a plain openai binding @ dial endpoint would actually fail on auth/path... but dialect-wise passable; the binding layer is about wire dialect, fine).

15:///    match the wire kind. A known endpoint of ANOTHER dialect
16:///    ([ProviderSpec.defaultBaseUrl], [sameEndpoint]-normalized) and a

19:///    hatch and is echoed in every report (E6: a genuinely
20:///    foreign-dialect endpoint behind a custom baseUrl passes only

26:///    endpoints always pass — there is nothing to check them against
27:///    (D2: the `unverified` marker territory, never a silent guess).

messages.preview: The `api` field is the true dialect. Let me fix the validators to compare API dialects (keeps the bench's `openai @ zai-endpoint` config valid, still catches the incident class):

blocks.text:
The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓
- openai-completions-kind binding @ codex endpoint: which spec? resolveCliProviderSpec('openai-completions', baseUrl: codex-url) → legacy rule: baseUrl != null → openai spec. api openai-completions vs spec(chatgpt).api responses → reject ✓

For the vendor-prefix rule (`zai/glm-...` on non-openai wire): compare prefix spec's API vs binding spec's API — `anthropic` binding + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`: anthropic-messages vs zai's openai-completions → reject ✓. And `openai/gpt-4o` on anthropic binding: openai api openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (good — that's also a real mismatch class). On openai-completions binding: equal apis → pass ✓. My current rule exempted openai-completions-bound wires entirely; comparing apis generalizes correctly: openrouter binding + `anthropic/claude-...` → apis equal (both openai-completions) → pass ✓.

For the model-family hint on a known endpoint: hint must map to an API DIALECT. Hints: claude → anthropic-messages; gemini → google-generative-ai; gpt/o1/o3/o4/chatgpt → openai-completions. Compare hint dialect vs endpoint-owning spec's api:
- gpt-5 + api.anthropic.com: openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (H2)
- claude-sonnet + api.openai.com: anthropic-messages vs openai-completions → reject. Hmm — is that a false positive? claude models via an OPENAI-compatible... api.openai.com does NOT serve claude models. Rejecting is correct!
- gemini-2.5-pro + openrouter endpoint: google-generative-ai vs openai-completions → REJECT. But `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` (prefixed) works on openrouter; BARE `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter? OpenRouter's ids are prefixed (`google/gemini-2.5-pro`) — bare `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter would 400. Hmm — but wait: my `_knownModels['openrouter']` list includes 'google/gemini-2.5-pro' (prefixed). Bare gemini on openrouter: unlikely to work. BUT — glm-... hmm no. What about copilot? Copilot serves claude/gpt models BARE over openai-completions wire (GitHub Models / Copilot API serves `claude-sonnet-4` etc.)! Copilot spec api is 'openai-completions', endpoint api.githubcopilot.com. A copilot binding + `claude-sonnet-4-5` (a REAL copilot model id!) → hint anthropic-messages vs copilot's openai-completions → FALSE POSITIVE — would break legit copilot usage. Damn.

Let me check the copilot model ids... The `_visionModel` mentions copilot; copilot models in the wild are like `claude-sonnet-4` — yes, bare claude ids are Copilot's model naming. Also the kimi coding endpoint serves `kimi-for-coding`... and DIAL deployments can be named anything (`anthropic/claude-...`? DIAL deployment names like `claude-...`? EPAM DIAL deployments are typically `gpt-4o`, `claude-...`-ish names too!).

So the bare-family rule is ONLY safe against endpoints that provably don't serve other families: api.anthropic.com serves ONLY claude models; api.openai.com serves ONLY gpt models; generativelanguage serves ONLY gemini. So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + gpt-5 → REJECT ✓ (H2!)
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + claude-* → pass
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + gemini-2.5-pro → REJECT ✓
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + claude-sonnet → REJECT — hmm, is api.openai.com ever a proxy for claude? No — OpenAI's own API. Correct to reject... unless a user points --base-url at api.openai.com running some gateway? They'd be reimplementing api.openai.com. Accept.
- endpoint openrouter/copilot/kimi/zai/dial/LAN → NO bare-family check (multi-family routers) → pass ✓ (copilot claude ids safe, DIAL safe).

So implement: `_canonicalFamilyDialect(endpoint)` → returns the family-dialect ONLY for the three single-family canonical endpoints (anthropic/openai/google specs where spec.name == the family owner). Better: a static map of canonical endpoints → their family wire-dialect: use the spec where the endpoint is the default AND the spec is the FAMILY OWNER (anthropic spec → anthropic-messages family; openai spec → openai-completions family; google spec → google-generative-ai family). Then reject when modelId's hint dialect != that family dialect. This keeps copilot (kind copilot, api openai-completions — but NOT the openai FAMILY owner) exempt. Wait — copilot's api IS openai-completions but its endpoint isn't api.openai.com so it's exempt from the bare check anyway. And wire⇄endpoint via api comparison for copilot: copilot binding @ api.openai.com? copilot api openai-completions == openai api → pass — hmm, copilot wire @ openai endpoint would actually need the copilot token exchange — but dialect-wise the wire is openai-completions-compatible. The endpoint-LOCKED check in startup already refuses copilot over foreign endpoints (endpointLocked). Fine.

Now the wire⇄endpoint api-comparison rule: binding spec api vs endpoint-owning spec X api. One more false-positive check: dial endpoint (ai-proxy.lab.epam.com, api openai-completions) + binding kind 'dial' → same spec → pass. Binding kind 'openai-completions' @ dial endpoint: legacy rule resolves openai spec, api openai-completions == dial api → pass. Correct (dial speaks openai-completions; DIAL needs the Api-Key header + path rewrite, handled by the dial adapter via kind — a plain openai binding @ dial endpoint would actually fail on auth/path... but dialect-wise passable; the binding layer is about wire dialect, fine).

zai endpoint + binding kind 'zai' → same spec → pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'kimi' → same spec pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'codemie'? codemie api openai-completions == kimi api → pass (dialect-compatible, endpoint/key layer sorts the rest). OK.

Let me now rewrite those two validators in the binding module and update my tests:
- Test 'a known endpoint of another dialect is rejected': anthropic @ api.openai.com → apis anthropic-messages vs openai-completions → reject ✓ (message must contain api.openai.com + anthropic).
- Test 'trailing-slash spelling of a foreign endpoint' (zai endpoint, trailing slash): anthropic binding @ zai endpoint → apis differ → reject ✓.
- Test 'gemini-2.5-pro on openrouter rejected' — I need to REVERSE this: openrouter is a multi-family router → bare gemini PASSES now. Update my test to expect PASS (and add a canonical-endpoint rejection test: gemini-2.5-pro @ api.openai.com/v1 → reject).
- The vendor-prefix test stays (zai/ on anthropic binding rejected via api mismatch).

Also update the binding doc comments to reflect api-dialect semantics.

1:/// The ONE validated provider+model identity (gh-1570): every way a
2:/// session picks its model — env preconfig, CLI flags, `/model`,
3:/// `/provider`, session restore, the provider queue, media slots, the
4:/// Flutter app settings — produces a [ProviderModelBinding] through
5:/// [ProviderModelBinding.resolve] or fails with an error naming BOTH
6:/// sides. A model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire
7:/// format, or API key.
8:///
9:/// The binding is the boundary INTO the already-correct resolved world
10:/// (`ModelRef.parse` requires a provider, `ModelRolesResolver` assembles
11:/// model+key+stream from one ref, `ProviderQueueEntry` carries its own
12:/// provider config). What it validates:
13:///
14:/// 1. *Wire ⇄ endpoint* — the endpoint's declared/known dialect must
15:///    match the wire kind. A known endpoint of ANOTHER dialect
16:///    ([ProviderSpec.defaultBaseUrl], [sameEndpoint]-normalized) and a
17:///    vendor-prefixed model id (`zai/glm-…`) riding a non-openai wire are
18:///    both rejections. An explicit `wire:` override is the only escape
19:///    hatch and is echoed in every report (E6: a genuinely
20:///    foreign-dialect endpoint behind a custom baseUrl passes only
21:///    through it).
22:/// 2. *Model ⇄ endpoint* — a model id whose family is KNOWN
23:///    ([modelFamilyWireHint]: `claude-*` is anthropic wire, `gemini-*`
24:///    google, `gpt-*`/`o1`/`o3`/`o4-*` openai-completions) is rejected on
25:///    a KNOWN endpoint of another dialect. Unknown ids and unknown
26:///    endpoints always pass — there is nothing to check them against
27:///    (D2: the `unverified` marker territory, never a silent guess).
28:/// 3. *Endpoint-shared wires* — `openai-completions` is six catalog
29:///    records (openai, openrouter, kimi, codemie, …). A binding on that
30:///    wire with NO record name and NO baseUrl has no identity at all and
31:///    is rejected instead of silently riding the legacy openrouter
32:///    default (M5: `OPENAI_API_KEY` sent to openrouter.ai).
33:/// 4. *Id shape and key indirection* — a model id carrying URL-ish or
34:///    control content is rejected before any endpoint call (E5); a key
35:///    ref must be an environment-variable NAME — key VALUES never enter
36:///    a binding (S3).
37:///
38:/// Pure Dart: no `dart:io`, no network — validation uses the provider
39:/// catalog only.

47:enum BindingProvenance {
48:  env,

52:  queue,
53:  media,
54:  app;

56:  /// The label reports render.

58:    BindingProvenance.env => 'env',

68:/// The complete identity of one provider+model choice: the catalog
69:/// record (or custom entry) name, the wire kind, the normalized endpoint,
70:/// the model id, the key's env indirection, and the provenance.
71:///
72:/// Construct ONLY through [ProviderModelBinding.resolve] — the single
73:/// validating constructor. Every field is immutable; equality covers the
74:/// identity fields (record, wire, endpoint, model, key ref) so a
75:/// persisted state can round-trip (I5) regardless of which entry point

77:final class ProviderModelBinding {
78:  ProviderModelBinding._({
79:    required this.recordName,
80:    required this.providerKind,
81:    required this.baseUrl,
82:    required this.modelId,
83:    required this.keyEnvRef,
84:    required this.provenance,
85:    required this.wireOverride,
86:  });
87:
88:  /// Resolves and VALIDATES one provider+model choice.
89:  ///
90:  /// [providerKind] is the caller's provider identity — a catalog name
91:  /// (`kimi`), an adapter kind (`anthropic`), or the shared
92:  /// `openai-completions` kind. [recordName] names the specific catalog
93:  /// or saved custom record when the caller knows it (endpoint-shared
94:  /// wires NEED it or an explicit [baseUrl]). [baseUrl] overrides the
95:  /// record's default endpoint; it is normalized (one trailing slash
96:  /// stripped). [wire] is the explicit `wire:` escape hatch: the declared
97:  /// adapter kind REPLACES the record's own wire kind and silences the
98:  /// dialect checks (the caller asserted the endpoint speaks it); the
99:  /// override is echoed by [echo]. [keyEnvRef] is the key's environment
100:  /// indirection — a NAME, never a value.
101:  ///
102:  /// Throws [ConfigException] naming the model, the endpoint, and the
103:  /// wire kind on every validation failure (I2).
104:  factory ProviderModelBinding.resolve({
105:    required String providerKind,
106:    required String modelId,
107:    String? baseUrl,
108:    String? recordName,
109:    String? keyEnvRef,
110:    BindingProvenance provenance = BindingProvenance.command,
111:    String? wire,
112:  }) {
113:    final name = recordName?.trim() ?? '';
114:    final rawKind = providerKind.trim().toLowerCase();
115:    if (rawKind.isEmpty) {
116:      throw const ConfigException(
117:        'provider model binding: no provider given — name the provider '
118:        'record (or adapter kind) the model rides',
119:      );
120:    }
121:    validateModelIdShape(modelId);
122:
123:    // The `wire:` escape hatch resolves FIRST: it is the adapter kind the
124:    // caller asserts the endpoint speaks, validated against the known
125:    // adapter kinds so a typo fails loud instead of inventing a wire.
126:    String? declaredWire;
127:    if (wire != null && wire.trim().isNotEmpty) {
128:      final declared = wire.trim().toLowerCase();
129:      final known = providerCatalog.values.any((spec) => spec.kind == declared);
130:      if (!known) {
131:        throw ConfigException(
132:          'unknown wire kind "$declared" — supported wire kinds: '
133:          '${providerCatalog.values.map((s) => s.kind).toSet().join(', ')}',
134:        );
135:      }
136:      declaredWire = declared;
137:    }
138:
139:    // The record: a catalog name/kind resolves to its spec (the ONE
140:    // both-identifier lookup). An unknown id with no wire override is a
141:    // fail-loud rejection — a binding names a real record or it names
142:    // nothing.
143:    final spec = resolveCliProviderSpec(
144:      name.isNotEmpty ? name : rawKind,
145:      baseUrl: baseUrl,
146:    );
147:    if (spec == null) {
148:      throw ConfigException(
149:        'unknown provider record "$providerKind" — a model binding names a '
150:        'provider catalog record (or adapter kind)',
151:      );
152:    }
153:    final wireKind = declaredWire ?? spec.kind;
154:    final override = declaredWire != null && declaredWire != spec.kind;
155:
156:    // Endpoint: explicit, else the record's own default. The endpoint-
157:    // shared kind with neither is identity-less — reject instead of
158:    // silently riding the legacy openrouter default (M5).
159:    final effectiveBaseUrl = _resolveBaseUrl(
160:      baseUrl: baseUrl,
161:      spec: spec,
162:      name: name,
163:      rawKind: rawKind,

blocks.text:
The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓
- openai-completions-kind binding @ codex endpoint: which spec? resolveCliProviderSpec('openai-completions', baseUrl: codex-url) → legacy rule: baseUrl != null → openai spec. api openai-completions vs spec(chatgpt).api responses → reject ✓

My current rule exempted openai-completions-bound wires entirely; comparing apis generalizes correctly: openrouter binding + `anthropic/claude-...` → apis equal (both openai-completions) → pass ✓.

For the model-family hint on a known endpoint: hint must map to an API DIALECT. Hints: claude → anthropic-messages; gemini → google-generative-ai; gpt/o1/o3/o4/chatgpt → openai-completions. Compare hint dialect vs endpoint-owning spec's api:

Copilot serves claude/gpt models BARE over openai-completions wire (GitHub Models / Copilot API serves `claude-sonnet-4` etc.)! A copilot binding + `claude-sonnet-4-5` (a REAL copilot model id!) → hint anthropic-messages vs copilot's openai-completions → FALSE POSITIVE — would break legit copilot usage. Damn.

Also the kimi coding endpoint serves `kimi-for-coding`... and DIAL deployments can be named anything (`anthropic/claude-...`? DIAL deployment names like `claude-...`? So the bare-family rule is ONLY safe against endpoints that provably don't serve other families: api.anthropic.com serves ONLY claude models; api.openai.com serves ONLY gpt models; generativelanguage serves ONLY gemini. So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:

The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓
- openai-completions-kind binding @ codex endpoint: which spec? resolveCliProviderSpec('openai-completions', baseUrl: codex-url) → legacy rule: baseUrl != null → openai spec. api openai-completions vs spec(chatgpt).api responses → reject ✓

For the model-family hint on a known endpoint: hint must map to an API DIALECT. Hints: claude → anthropic-messages; gemini → google-generative-ai; gpt/o1/o3/o4/chatgpt → openai-completions. Compare hint dialect vs endpoint-owning spec's api:

blocks.text:
The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓
- openai-completions-kind binding @ codex endpoint: which spec? resolveCliProviderSpec('openai-completions', baseUrl: codex-url) → legacy rule: baseUrl != null → openai spec. api openai-completions vs spec(chatgpt).api responses → reject ✓

For the vendor-prefix rule (`zai/glm-...` on non-openai wire): compare prefix spec's API vs binding spec's API — `anthropic` binding + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`: anthropic-messages vs zai's openai-completions → reject ✓. And `openai/gpt-4o` on anthropic binding: openai api openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (good — that's also a real mismatch class). On openai-completions binding: equal apis → pass ✓. My current rule exempted openai-completions-bound wires entirely; comparing apis generalizes correctly: openrouter binding + `anthropic/claude-...` → apis equal (both openai-completions) → pass ✓.

For the model-family hint on a known endpoint: hint must map to an API DIALECT. Hints: claude → anthropic-messages; gemini → google-generative-ai; gpt/o1/o3/o4/chatgpt → openai-completions. Compare hint dialect vs endpoint-owning spec's api:
- gpt-5 + api.anthropic.com: openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (H2)
- claude-sonnet + api.openai.com: anthropic-messages vs openai-completions → reject. Hmm — is that a false positive? claude models via an OPENAI-compatible... api.openai.com does NOT serve claude models. Rejecting is correct!
- gemini-2.5-pro + openrouter endpoint: google-generative-ai vs openai-completions → REJECT. But `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` (prefixed) works on openrouter; BARE `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter? OpenRouter's ids are prefixed (`google/gemini-2.5-pro`) — bare `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter would 400. Hmm — but wait: my `_knownModels['openrouter']` list includes 'google/gemini-2.5-pro' (prefixed). Bare gemini on openrouter: unlikely to work. BUT — glm-... hmm no. What about copilot? Copilot serves claude/gpt models BARE over openai-completions wire (GitHub Models / Copilot API serves `claude-sonnet-4` etc.)! Copilot spec api is 'openai-completions', endpoint api.githubcopilot.com. A copilot binding + `claude-sonnet-4-5` (a REAL copilot model id!) → hint anthropic-messages vs copilot's openai-completions → FALSE POSITIVE — would break legit copilot usage. Damn.

Let me check the copilot model ids... The `_visionModel` mentions copilot; copilot models in the wild are like `claude-sonnet-4` — yes, bare claude ids are Copilot's model naming. Also the kimi coding endpoint serves `kimi-for-coding`... and DIAL deployments can be named anything (`anthropic/claude-...`? DIAL deployment names like `claude-...`? EPAM DIAL deployments are typically `gpt-4o`, `claude-...`-ish names too!).

So the bare-family rule is ONLY safe against endpoints that provably don't serve other families: api.anthropic.com serves ONLY claude models; api.openai.com serves ONLY gpt models; generativelanguage serves ONLY gemini. So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + gpt-5 → REJECT ✓ (H2!)
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + claude-* → pass
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + gemini-2.5-pro → REJECT ✓
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + claude-sonnet → REJECT — hmm, is api.openai.com ever a proxy for claude? No — OpenAI's own API. Correct to reject... unless a user points --base-url at api.openai.com running some gateway? They'd be reimplementing api.openai.com. Accept.
- endpoint openrouter/copilot/kimi/zai/dial/LAN → NO bare-family check (multi-family routers) → pass ✓ (copilot claude ids safe, DIAL safe).

So implement: `_canonicalFamilyDialect(endpoint)` → returns the family-dialect ONLY for the three single-family canonical endpoints (anthropic/openai/google specs where spec.name == the family owner). Better: a static map of canonical endpoints → their family wire-dialect: use the spec where the endpoint is the default AND the spec is the FAMILY OWNER (anthropic spec → anthropic-messages family; openai spec → openai-completions family; google spec → google-generative-ai family). Then reject when modelId's hint dialect != that family dialect. This keeps copilot (kind copilot, api openai-completions — but NOT the openai FAMILY owner) exempt. Wait — copilot's api IS openai-completions but its endpoint isn't api.openai.com so it's exempt from the bare check anyway. And wire⇄endpoint via api comparison for copilot: copilot binding @ api.openai.com? copilot api openai-completions == openai api → pass — hmm, copilot wire @ openai endpoint would actually need the copilot token exchange — but dialect-wise the wire is openai-completions-compatible. The endpoint-LOCKED check in startup already refuses copilot over foreign endpoints (endpointLocked). Fine.

Now the wire⇄endpoint api-comparison rule: binding spec api vs endpoint-owning spec X api. One more false-positive check: dial endpoint (ai-proxy.lab.epam.com, api openai-completions) + binding kind 'dial' → same spec → pass. Binding kind 'openai-completions' @ dial endpoint: legacy rule resolves openai spec, api openai-completions == dial api → pass. Correct (dial speaks openai-completions; DIAL needs the Api-Key header + path rewrite, handled by the dial adapter via kind — a plain openai binding @ dial endpoint would actually fail on auth/path... but dialect-wise passable; the binding layer is about wire dialect, fine).

zai endpoint + binding kind 'zai' → same spec → pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'kimi' → same spec pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'codemie'? codemie api openai-completions == kimi api → pass (dialect-compatible, endpoint/key layer sorts the rest). OK.

Let me now rewrite those two validators in the binding module and update my tests:
- Test 'a known endpoint of another dialect is rejected': anthropic @ api.openai.com → apis anthropic-messages vs openai-completions → reject ✓ (message must contain api.openai.com + anthropic).
- Test 'trailing-slash spelling of a foreign endpoint' (zai endpoint, trailing slash): anthropic binding @ zai endpoint → apis differ → reject ✓.
- Test 'gemini-2.5-pro on openrouter rejected' — I need to REVERSE this: openrouter is a multi-family router → bare gemini PASSES now. Update my test to expect PASS (and add a canonical-endpoint rejection test: gemini-2.5-pro @ api.openai.com/v1 → reject).
- The vendor-prefix test stays (zai/ on anthropic binding rejected via api mismatch).

Also update the binding doc comments to reflect api-dialect semantics.

The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓
- openai-completions-kind binding @ codex endpoint: which spec? resolveCliProviderSpec('openai-completions', baseUrl: codex-url) → legacy rule: baseUrl != null → openai spec. api openai-completions vs spec(chatgpt).api responses → reject ✓

For the vendor-prefix rule (`zai/glm-...` on non-openai wire): compare prefix spec's API vs binding spec's API — `anthropic` binding + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`: anthropic-messages vs zai's openai-completions → reject ✓. And `openai/gpt-4o` on anthropic binding: openai api openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (good — that's also a real mismatch class). On openai-completions binding: equal apis → pass ✓. My current rule exempted openai-completions-bound wires entirely; comparing apis generalizes correctly: openrouter binding + `anthropic/claude-...` → apis equal (both openai-completions) → pass ✓.

For the model-family hint on a known endpoint: hint must map to an API DIALECT. Hints: claude → anthropic-messages; gemini → google-generative-ai; gpt/o1/o3/o4/chatgpt → openai-completions. Compare hint dialect vs endpoint-owning spec's api:
- gpt-5 + api.anthropic.com: openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (H2)
- claude-sonnet + api.openai.com: anthropic-messages vs openai-completions → reject. Hmm — is that a false positive? claude models via an OPENAI-compatible... api.openai.com does NOT serve claude models. Rejecting is correct!
- gemini-2.5-pro + openrouter endpoint: google-generative-ai vs openai-completions → REJECT. But `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` (prefixed) works on openrouter; BARE `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter? OpenRouter's ids are prefixed (`google/gemini-2.5-pro`) — bare `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter would 400. Hmm — but wait: my `_knownModels['openrouter']` list includes 'google/gemini-2.5-pro' (prefixed). Bare gemini on openrouter: unlikely to work. BUT — glm-... hmm no. What about copilot? Copilot serves claude/gpt models BARE over openai-completions wire (GitHub Models / Copilot API serves `claude-sonnet-4` etc.)! Copilot spec api is 'openai-completions', endpoint api.githubcopilot.com. A copilot binding + `claude-sonnet-4-5` (a REAL copilot model id!) → hint anthropic-messages vs copilot's openai-completions → FALSE POSITIVE — would break legit copilot usage. Damn.

Let me check the copilot model ids... The `_visionModel` mentions copilot; copilot models in the wild are like `claude-sonnet-4` — yes, bare claude ids are Copilot's model naming. Also the kimi coding endpoint serves `kimi-for-coding`... and DIAL deployments can be named anything (`anthropic/claude-...`? DIAL deployment names like `claude-...`? EPAM DIAL deployments are typically `gpt-4o`, `claude-...`-ish names too!).

So the bare-family rule is ONLY safe against endpoints that provably don't serve other families: api.anthropic.com serves ONLY claude models; api.openai.com serves ONLY gpt models; generativelanguage serves ONLY gemini. So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + gpt-5 → REJECT ✓ (H2!)
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + claude-* → pass
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + gemini-2.5-pro → REJECT ✓
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + claude-sonnet → REJECT — hmm, is api.openai.com ever a proxy for claude? No — OpenAI's own API. Correct to reject... unless a user points --base-url at api.openai.com running some gateway? They'd be reimplementing api.openai.com. Accept.
- endpoint openrouter/copilot/kimi/zai/dial/LAN → NO bare-family check (multi-family routers) → pass ✓ (copilot claude ids safe, DIAL safe).

So implement: `_canonicalFamilyDialect(endpoint)` → returns the family-dialect ONLY for the three single-family canonical endpoints (anthropic/openai/google specs where spec.name == the family owner). Better: a static map of canonical endpoints → their family wire-dialect: use the spec where the endpoint is the default AND the spec is the FAMILY OWNER (anthropic spec → anthropic-messages family; openai spec → openai-completions family; google spec → google-generative-ai family). Correct (dial speaks openai-completions; DIAL needs the Api-Key header + path rewrite, handled by the dial adapter via kind — a plain openai binding @ dial endpoint would actually fail on auth/path... but dialect-wise passable; the binding layer is about wire dialect, fine).

zai endpoint + binding kind 'zai' → same spec → pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'kimi' → same spec pass ✓. kimi endpoint + kind 'codemie'? codemie api openai-completions == kimi api → pass (dialect-compatible, endpoint/key layer sorts the rest). OK.

The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓

- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'

If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓

Hmm — but wait: my `_knownModels['openrouter']` list includes 'google/gemini-2.5-pro' (prefixed). Bare gemini on openrouter: unlikely to work. BUT — glm-... hmm no. What about copilot? Copilot serves claude/gpt models BARE over openai-completions wire (GitHub Models / Copilot API serves `claude-sonnet-4` etc.)! Also the kimi coding endpoint serves `kimi-for-coding`... and DIAL deployments can be named anything (`anthropic/claude-...`? DIAL deployment names like `claude-...`? So the bare-family rule is ONLY safe against endpoints that provably don't serve other families: api.anthropic.com serves ONLY claude models; api.openai.com serves ONLY gpt models; generativelanguage serves ONLY gemini. So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:

4:/// Flutter app settings — produces a [ProviderModelBinding] through

6:/// sides. A model can never again silently ride a foreign endpoint, wire
7:/// format, or API key.

9:/// The binding is the boundary INTO the already-correct resolved world
10:/// (`ModelRef.parse` requires a provider, `ModelRolesResolver` assembles
11:/// model+key+stream from one ref, `ProviderQueueEntry` carries its own
12:/// provider config). What it validates:
13:///
14:/// 1. *Wire ⇄ endpoint* — the endpoint's declared/known dialect must
15:///    match the wire kind. A known endpoint of ANOTHER dialect
16:///    ([ProviderSpec.defaultBaseUrl], [sameEndpoint]-normalized) and a
17:///    vendor-prefixed model id (`zai/glm-…`) riding a non-openai wire are
18:///    both rejections. An explicit `wire:` override is the only escape
19:///    hatch and is echoed in every report (E6: a genuinely
20:///    foreign-dialect endpoint behind a custom baseUrl passes only
21:///    through it).
22:/// 2. *Model ⇄ endpoint* — a model id whose family is KNOWN
23:///    ([modelFamilyWireHint]: `claude-*` is anthropic wire, `gemini-*`
24:///    google, `gpt-*`/`o1`/`o3`/`o4-*` openai-completions) is rejected on
25:///    a KNOWN endpoint of another dialect. Unknown ids and unknown
26:///    endpoints always pass — there is nothing to check them against
27:///    (D2: the `unverified` marker territory, never a silent guess).
28:/// 3. *Endpoint-shared wires* — `openai-completions` is six catalog
29:///    records (openai, openrouter, kimi, codemie, …). A binding on that
30:///    wire with NO record name and NO baseUrl has no identity at all and
31:///    is rejected instead of silently riding the legacy openrouter
32:///    default (M5: `OPENAI_API_KEY` sent to openrouter.ai).
33:/// 4. *Id shape and key indirection* — a model id carrying URL-ish or
34:///    control content is rejected before any endpoint call (E5); a key
35:///    ref must be an environment-variable NAME — key VALUES never enter

47:enum BindingProvenance {

53:  media,
54:  app;

58:    BindingProvenance.env => 'env',

68:/// The complete identity of one provider+model choice: the catalog
69:/// record (or custom entry) name, the wire kind, the normalized endpoint,
70:/// the model id, the key's env indirection, and the provenance.
71:///
72:/// Construct ONLY through [ProviderModelBinding.resolve] — the single
73:/// validating constructor. Every field is immutable; equality covers the
74:/// identity fields (record, wire, endpoint, model, key ref) so a

77:final class ProviderModelBinding {
78:  ProviderModelBinding._({
79:    required this.recordName,
80:    required this.providerKind,
81:    required this.baseUrl,
82:    required this.modelId,
83:    required this.keyEnvRef,
84:    required this.provenance,
85:    required this.wireOverride,
86:  });
87:
88:  /// Resolves and VALIDATES one provider+model choice.
89:  ///
90:  /// [providerKind] is the caller's provider identity — a catalog name
91:  /// (`kimi`), an adapter kind (`anthropic`), or the shared
92:  /// `openai-completions` kind. [recordName] names the specific catalog
93:  /// or saved custom record when the caller knows it (endpoint-shared
94:  /// wires NEED it or an explicit [baseUrl]). [baseUrl] overrides the
95:  /// record's default endpoint; it is normalized (one trailing slash
96:  /// stripped). [wire] is the explicit `wire:` escape hatch: the declared
97:  /// adapter kind REPLACES the record's own wire kind and silences the
98:  /// dialect checks (the caller asserted the endpoint speaks it); the
99:  /// override is echoed by [echo]. [keyEnvRef] is the key's environment
100:  /// indirection — a NAME, never a value.
101:  ///
102:  /// Throws [ConfigException] naming the model, the endpoint, and the
103:  /// wire kind on every validation failure (I2).
104:  factory ProviderModelBinding.resolve({
105:    required String providerKind,
106:    required String modelId,
107:    String? baseUrl,
108:    String? recordName,
109:    String? keyEnvRef,
110:    BindingProvenance provenance = BindingProvenance.command,
111:    String? wire,
112:  }) {
113:    final name = recordName?.trim() ?? '';
114:    final rawKind = providerKind.trim().toLowerCase();
115:    if (rawKind.isEmpty) {
116:      throw const ConfigException(
117:        'provider model binding: no provider given — name the provider '
118:        'record (or adapter kind) the model rides',
119:      );
120:    }
121:    validateModelIdShape(modelId);
122:
123:    // The `wire:` escape hatch resolves FIRST: it is the adapter kind the
124:    // caller asserts the endpoint speaks, validated against the known
125:    // adapter kinds so a typo fails loud instead of inventing a wire.
126:    String? declaredWire;
127:    if (wire != null && wire.trim().isNotEmpty) {
128:      final declared = wire.trim().toLowerCase();
129:      final known = providerCatalog.values.any((spec) => spec.kind == declared);
130:      if (!known) {
131:        throw ConfigException(
132:          'unknown wire kind "$declared" — supported wire kinds: '
133:          '${providerCatalog.values.map((s) => s.kind).toSet().join(', ')}',
134:        );
135:      }
136:      declaredWire = declared;
137:    }
138:
139:    // The record: a catalog name/kind resolves to its spec (the ONE
140:    // both-identifier lookup). An unknown id with no wire override is a
141:    // fail-loud rejection — a binding names a real record or it names
142:    // nothing.

blocks.text:
The api dialect values: `openai-completions`, `responses` (chatgpt-codex), `anthropic-messages` (anthropicMessagesApi), `google-generative-ai`. 

So I need a mapping from adapter KIND → endpoint dialect for the binding's wire:
- kind 'anthropic' → api 'anthropic-messages'
- kind 'google' → 'google-generative-ai'
- all other kinds (openai-completions, zai, minimax, dial, copilot, aiin, kimi, codemie, openrouter, openai, chatgpt-codex 'responses'!) 

Hmm — chatgpt-codex kind: api 'responses'. Its endpoint chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex speaks the Responses wire. If a binding kind is 'openai-completions' with baseUrl codex endpoint → dialect mismatch (openai-completions vs responses) → reject. Good. But binding kind 'chatgpt-codex' (spec chatgpt, kind chatgpt-codex, api responses) @ codex endpoint: endpoint spec is the same spec → same api → pass.

The dialect for a WIRE KIND: resolve the kind → the spec → but shared kinds have per-spec apis... The wire⇄endpoint check simplifies to: **compare the bound RECORD's api with the ENDPOINT-OWNING record's api**. When baseUrl matches spec X's default endpoint: binding spec's `api` must equal X's `api`. When the binding spec IS X (same record), trivially equal. 

- FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai @ zai endpoint: spec(openai).api = openai-completions == spec(zai).api = openai-completions → pass ✓
- anthropic @ api.openai.com: anthropic-messages != openai-completions → reject ✓
- openai-completions-kind binding @ codex endpoint: which spec? resolveCliProviderSpec('openai-completions', baseUrl: codex-url) → legacy rule: baseUrl != null → openai spec. api openai-completions vs spec(chatgpt).api responses → reject ✓

For the vendor-prefix rule (`zai/glm-...` on non-openai wire): compare prefix spec's API vs binding spec's API — `anthropic` binding + `zai/glm-5.3-flashx`: anthropic-messages vs zai's openai-completions → reject ✓. And `openai/gpt-4o` on anthropic binding: openai api openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (good — that's also a real mismatch class). On openai-completions binding: equal apis → pass ✓. My current rule exempted openai-completions-bound wires entirely; comparing apis generalizes correctly: openrouter binding + `anthropic/claude-...` → apis equal (both openai-completions) → pass ✓.

For the model-family hint on a known endpoint: hint must map to an API DIALECT. Hints: claude → anthropic-messages; gemini → google-generative-ai; gpt/o1/o3/o4/chatgpt → openai-completions. Compare hint dialect vs endpoint-owning spec's api:
- gpt-5 + api.anthropic.com: openai-completions vs anthropic-messages → reject ✓ (H2)
- claude-sonnet + api.openai.com: anthropic-messages vs openai-completions → reject. Hmm — is that a false positive? claude models via an OPENAI-compatible... api.openai.com does NOT serve claude models. Rejecting is correct!
- gemini-2.5-pro + openrouter endpoint: google-generative-ai vs openai-completions → REJECT. But `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` (prefixed) works on openrouter; BARE `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter? OpenRouter's ids are prefixed (`google/gemini-2.5-pro`) — bare `gemini-2.5-pro` on openrouter would 400. Hmm — but wait: my `_knownModels['openrouter']` list includes 'google/gemini-2.5-pro' (prefixed). Bare gemini on openrouter: unlikely to work. BUT — glm-... hmm no. What about copilot? Copilot serves claude/gpt models BARE over openai-completions wire (GitHub Models / Copilot API serves `claude-sonnet-4` etc.)! Copilot spec api is 'openai-completions', endpoint api.githubcopilot.com. A copilot binding + `claude-sonnet-4-5` (a REAL copilot model id!) → hint anthropic-messages vs copilot's openai-completions → FALSE POSITIVE — would break legit copilot usage. Damn.

Let me check the copilot model ids... The `_visionModel` mentions copilot; copilot models in the wild are like `claude-sonnet-4` — yes, bare claude ids are Copilot's model naming. Also the kimi coding endpoint serves `kimi-for-coding`... and DIAL deployments can be named anything (`anthropic/claude-...`? DIAL deployment names like `claude-...`? EPAM DIAL deployments are typically `gpt-4o`, `claude-...`-ish names too!).

So the bare-family rule is ONLY safe against endpoints that provably don't serve other families: api.anthropic.com serves ONLY claude models; api.openai.com serves ONLY gpt models; generativelanguage serves ONLY gemini. So restrict the bare-family check to the FAMILY'S OWN-PROVIDER mismatch: hint fires only when the endpoint is the CANONICAL endpoint of a DIFFERENT family — i.e., endpoint ∈ {api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com/v1, generativelanguage...} and the model family does NOT belong to that endpoint's family:
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + gpt-5 → REJECT ✓ (H2!)
- endpoint api.anthropic.com + claude-* → pass
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + gemini-2.5-pro → REJECT ✓
- endpoint api.openai.com/v1 + claude-sonnet → REJECT — hmm, is api.openai.com ever a proxy for claude? No — OpenAI's own API. Correct to reject... unless a user points --base-url at api.openai.com running some gateway? They'd be reimplementing api.openai.com. Accept.
- endpoint openrouter/copilot/kimi/zai/dial/LAN → NO bare-family check (multi-family routers) → pass ✓ (copilot claude ids safe, DIAL safe).

So implement: `_canonicalFamilyDialect(endpoint)` → returns the family-dialect ONLY for the three single-family canonical endpoints (anthropic/openai/google specs where spec.name == the family owner). Better: a static map of canonical endpoints → their family wire-dialect: use the spec where the endpoint is the default AND the spec is the FAMILY OWNER (anthropic spec → anthropic-messages family; openai spec → openai-completions family; google spec → google-generative-ai family). Then reject when modelId's hint dialect != that family dialect. This keeps copilot (kind copilot, api openai-completions — but NOT the openai FAMILY owner) exempt. Wait — copilot's api IS openai-completions but its endpoint isn't api.openai.com so it's exempt from the bare check anyway. And wire⇄endpoint via api comparison for copilot: copilot binding @ api.openai.com? copilot api openai-completions == openai api → pass — hmm, copilot wire @ openai endpoint would actually need the copilot token exchange — but dialect-wise the wire is openai-completions-compatible.
